brief.meaningEn: Become or make something less fast, intense or demanding, rather than necessarily stop it.
brief.meaningZh: 使速度、強度或要求降低，或變得較輕鬆，但不一定完全停止。
brief.grammar: the pressure/rain eases off; ease off after a deadline; ease off on the questioning. Identify the intensity being reduced and what still continues.
brief.register: Common phrasal verb for a reduction in intensity. The change can be deliberate or observed; it does not automatically mean giving up a goal or removing every obligation.
brief.boundaryZh: 強度減弱不等於完全停止，也不表示問題全已解決或不再關心；要說清減少哪部分，以及甚麼仍會繼續。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可以減輕壓力，同時保留必要的核查；也可以減少追問，同時繼續支持別人，不以強度作為投入的唯一證據。
brief.outcomeZh: 能自然表達強度減輕，以及仍然繼續的部分，分清計劃、實際過程與完全停止。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The team can ease off after the deadline.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 49, table 1, row 2; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: After the exhibition deadline, we could ease off on late-night printing, but the agreed returns still needed checking; the coordinator proposed a shorter daytime session rather than abandoning the remaining work.
listening.zh: 展覽限期過後，我們可以減少深夜印刷，但先前議定的物品歸還仍需要核對；統籌建議改為較短的日間工作時段，而不是放棄餘下工作。
listening.promptZh: 減少的是哪部分？還有甚麼需要處理？

options.en: The late-night intensity could reduce while a shorter session handled the remaining checks.
options.zh: 深夜工作的強度可以降低，餘下核查則可在較短的時段處理。

options.en: Every remaining return had been cancelled because the deadline passed.
options.zh: 因為限期已過，所有餘下的物品歸還都已取消。

options.en: The coordinator proposed adding another late-night printing shift.
options.zh: 統籌建議再加一班深夜印刷工作。

options.en: The coordinator proposed splitting the remaining checks among several late-night sessions.
options.zh: 統籌建議把餘下核查分到幾個深夜時段處理。

listening.explanationZh: 建議是減少深夜工作，並在較短的日間時段完成仍需處理的核查；不是取消歸還、增加夜班或繼續把核查分到深夜。

reply.promptZh: 統籌為甚麼建議改用較短的日間工作時段？
reply.promptEn: Why did the coordinator suggest a shorter daytime session?

options.en: We could ease off after the deadline while still checking the agreed returns.
options.zh: 限期過後，我們可以降低工作強度，同時核對議定的物品歸還。

options.en: The intense printing period had passed, but a limited amount of follow-up remained.
options.zh: 密集的印刷階段已過，但仍有少量跟進工作。

options.en: A smaller session matched the remaining work without requiring another late night.
options.zh: 較短的時段已能配合餘下工作，不需要再做到深夜。

options.en: The team wanted to reduce the demand without treating the unfinished checks as optional.
options.zh: 小組想減輕負擔，但不把未完成的核查當作可以省略。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋了為何可以降低強度，同時保留餘下責任。

scene.promptZh: 敘述說雨勢減弱，但仍下着細雨，人物繼續站在有遮蓋的地方；旁人卻把 ease off 理解為雨已完全停止。哪句最準確？

options.en: The rain has eased off, but lighter rain is still falling in this account.
options.zh: 雨勢已減弱，但這段敘述中仍在下細雨。

options.en: The description establishes that no rain is falling anywhere at that moment.
options.zh: 這段描述證明，那一刻任何地方都沒有下雨。

options.en: The rain grew heavier, which is why the character described a reduction.
options.zh: 雨勢變得更大，所以人物說雨勢已減弱。

scene.explanationZh: ease off 可以形容雨勢減弱，但不表示雨已完全停止，也不是說雨勢變強。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能從 ease off 的「減弱」意思推論出來？

options.en: Intensity becomes lower.
options.zh: 強度有所降低。

options.en: The activity or pressure must have stopped completely.
options.zh: 活動或壓力必定已完全停止。

options.en: Some work or support can continue at a lower level.
options.zh: 部分工作或支援仍可以較低的強度繼續。

contrast.explanationZh: 強度降低和完全停止是不同的情況。

dialogue.promptZh: 同事問：「你說 ease off，是指物品歸還的核查也不用做嗎？」那些核查仍是大家已議定的工作。哪個回應最好？

options.en: No, I mean easing off on late-night work, not the agreed checks; we can do those in the shorter session.
options.zh: 不是，我是指減少深夜工作，而不是省去議定的核查；那些可以在較短的時段處理。

options.en: Yes, reducing the intensity means none of the returns matters any longer.
options.zh: 是的，降低強度表示物品歸還已經不再重要。

options.en: I am asking for longer late-night shifts, rather than a reduction.
options.zh: 我是在要求更長的深夜班，而不是減少工作強度。

dialogue.explanationZh: 直接說清減少哪部分，以及如何保留原有責任，不把降低強度誤解為取消工作。

speaking.en: I want to ease off on the pressure, while keeping the support and the checks we have actually agreed.
speaking.zh: 我想減輕壓力，同時保留我們實際議定的支援及核查。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說清想減少甚麼，以及仍會保留甚麼。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你一直追問朋友何時寫完故事，她說現在每次聊天都像交代進度。你想道歉並減少催問，先問她想要怎樣的支持，而不是不再關心她。用一至兩句英文寫出實際訊息。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出真誠的道歉及支持邀請，減少追問帶來的壓力，同時表達關心；讓朋友自行選擇分享時間，不替她解釋沉默的意思。

examples.en: I am sorry my repeated questions have made our chats feel like progress reports; I will ease off on asking when the story will be finished. I still care about your writing, so please tell me what kind of support you would welcome.
examples.zh: 對不起，我反覆追問，令我們的聊天像進度報告；我會減少詢問故事何時完成。我仍關心你的寫作，所以請告訴我，你希望得到哪種支持。

examples.en: I need to ease off rather than turn every conversation into a deadline check. I would like to listen when you want to share, without treating silence as a request for another reminder.
examples.zh: 我需要減少追問，而不是把每次談話都變成限期核查。你想分享時，我願意聽；我不會把你的沉默當作要求再提醒一次。

glossary.en: I still care about your writing
what kind of support you would welcome

takeaways.en: The group agreed to ease off on extra rehearsals while keeping the one session needed for the opening.
takeaways.zh: 小組同意減少額外綵排，同時保留開幕所需的那一節。

takeaways.en: She eased off on the questions and asked what support her friend actually wanted.
takeaways.zh: 她減少追問，改為詢問朋友實際想得到甚麼支持。

titleZh: 像踏着油門般加快推進

brief.meaningEn: Using a driving image to describe maintaining or pressing for rapid activity or growth.
brief.meaningZh: 用駕駛的意象，形容維持或推動快速的活動及發展。
brief.grammar: have/keep its foot on the accelerator; my/their foot on the accelerator. A group or economy may be personified; the phrase alone does not mean literal driving or establish outside coercion.
brief.register: Productive driving metaphor. Fast pace or expansion is separate from quality, consent and sustainable capacity; apparent speed does not show every person wants it.
brief.boundaryZh: 加快步伐不保證成功，也不一定是受到外力強迫；要指出哪些行動顯示加速，以及哪些條件仍待確認。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把項目增加當作所有人都已同意，或每項成果都會更好；這個駕駛意象也不是實際的車速指令。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體的快速推進說明意象，分清步伐、動機及尚未確定的成效。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The economy seems to have its foot on the accelerator.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 49, table 1, row 3; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The festival committee seemed to have its foot on the accelerator, announcing three new sessions before checking rooms or volunteers; the programme was growing quickly, but the practical arrangements had not caught up.
listening.zh: 節慶委員會彷彿一直踩着油門，還未確認房間及義工人手，就宣布增加三項活動；節目迅速擴展，但實際安排還未跟上。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼細節支持加速的意象？哪些配套還未跟上？

options.en: New sessions were announced quickly before rooms and volunteers were checked.
options.zh: 委員會很快宣布新活動，但房間及義工人手還未確認。

options.en: Every room and volunteer had been confirmed before any new announcement.
options.zh: 在任何新公告發布前，所有房間及義工人手都已確認。

options.en: The committee had cancelled all expansion and was closing the existing programme.
options.zh: 委員會已取消一切擴展，並正在結束原有節目。

options.en: Each new session had already been tested with participants before the announcement.
options.zh: 每項新活動在宣布前，都已讓參加者試行過。

listening.explanationZh: 活動宣布得很快，但配套仍待確認，這支持了加速推進的意象；並不是配套全已備妥，或活動已先試行。

reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼把委員會的做法比作踩着油門？
reply.promptEn: Why did you compare the committee’s approach to pressing an accelerator?

options.en: It had its foot on the accelerator by announcing more sessions before checking the support for them.
options.zh: 委員會還未確認支援，就宣布更多活動，彷彿一直踩着油門。

options.en: The programme expanded faster than the practical arrangements were being confirmed.
options.zh: 節目擴展的速度，比實際安排獲確認的速度更快。

options.en: Three additions were announced while room and volunteer questions remained open.
options.zh: 房間及義工人手尚未確定時，就已宣布增加三項活動。

options.en: The pace of new commitments was the focus, not a completed assessment of their quality.
options.zh: 形容的重點是迅速增加承諾，而不是說活動品質已經評估妥當。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋了快速承諾與配套之間的落差，不把速度當作成效。

scene.promptZh: 同一委員會後來暫停增加活動，先逐項跟義工確認可承擔的工作量；你想準確描述目前不再急速推進的情況。哪句最好？

options.en: It is not keeping its foot on the accelerator now; it has paused additions to examine the capacity.
options.zh: 委員會現在不再一直踩着油門，而是暫停增加活動，先檢視可承擔的工作量。

options.en: The pause means three more sessions have already been added without discussion.
options.zh: 這次暫停表示，委員會已在沒有討論的情況下再加三項活動。

options.en: The account says every volunteer has committed to all the new sessions.
options.zh: 敘述說，每位義工都已承諾參與所有新增活動。

scene.explanationZh: 目前是先確認容量，而不是繼續加速；資料沒有說又加了活動，也沒有說所有人都已答應。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能從 its foot on the accelerator 的活動意象推論出來？

options.en: A group is pushing ahead at a rapid pace.
options.zh: 一個團隊正在快速推進。

options.en: Every new commitment is guaranteed to work well.
options.zh: 每項新增承諾都保證能順利落實。

options.en: The account can still question whether support has kept up.
options.zh: 仍然可以追問支援是否跟得上。

contrast.explanationZh: 加快步伐不保證品質，也不代表容量已經足夠。

dialogue.promptZh: 義工問：「活動這麼快就宣布了，是不是房間和人手都已確認？」目前那些安排仍未確認。哪個回答最好？

options.en: The committee has its foot on the accelerator, but those arrangements are still open; let us check before accepting another commitment.
options.zh: 委員會彷彿一直踩着油門，但那些安排仍未定；接受另一項承諾前，先確認清楚吧。

options.en: Yes, the speed of the announcements confirms that every practical detail is settled.
options.zh: 是的，公告發布得快，就證明每項實際細節都已定下來。

options.en: No new sessions have been announced, so there is no expansion to discuss.
options.zh: 目前沒有宣布任何新活動，所以沒有擴展的事情需要討論。

dialogue.explanationZh: 快速宣布與配套獲確認是兩回事；不能由速度推斷一切已定，也不能否認已公布的新增活動。

speaking.en: We have kept our foot on the accelerator, but I want to check what people can manage before adding another promise.
speaking.zh: 我們一直像踩着油門般推進，但再加一項承諾前，我想先確認大家能承擔多少。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清推進的步伐與實際可承擔的工作量。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫小說中一位導演給演員的道歉信。他為了趕出新劇，一直增加演出，沒有問演員想保留的學習及家庭時間；如今想承認自己推得太快，先聽每人能承擔多少，而不是再次替他們決定下一輪安排。用一至兩句英文寫出信的內容。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以道歉信承擔自己過快作承諾的責任，先問演員的容量及優先考慮，再共同決定；不把加速當成全體同意，也不未問便替他們取消安排。

examples.en: I have kept my foot on the accelerator by promising more performances before asking what you could manage, and I am sorry. Before the next round is agreed, I want to hear each person’s limits and priorities rather than decide for you again.
examples.zh: 我還未問你們能承擔多少，就不斷承諾更多演出，一直像踩着油門，實在很抱歉。下一輪安排議定前，我想聽各人的界線及優先考慮，不再替你們作決定。

examples.en: With my foot on the accelerator, I treated a growing programme as if it meant everyone wanted the same pace. I need to ask about your commitments before we decide together what the next round should contain.
examples.zh: 我一直踩着油門，把節目增加當作大家都想以同樣速度推進。共同決定下一輪應包含甚麼前，我需要先了解你們已有的承諾。

glossary.zh: 各人的界線及優先考慮

takeaways.en: The project had its foot on the accelerator, but its growing list of promises still needed people and time behind it.
takeaways.zh: 項目彷彿一直踩着油門，但不斷增加的承諾仍需要人手及時間支持。

takeaways.en: She kept her foot on the accelerator until a colleague asked which commitments had actually been agreed.
takeaways.zh: 她一直踩着油門推進，直到同事問哪些承諾實際上已獲同意。

titleZh: 與時間競賽、趕在限時前

brief.meaningEn: An effort to complete something before time runs out, with a strong sense of time pressure.
brief.meaningZh: 努力在時間用完前完成某事，帶有強烈的限時壓力。
brief.grammar: become/be a race against the clock; face a race against the clock to do something. The race is figurative, not necessarily a contest against other people.
brief.register: Common time-pressure idiom. It does not say the task succeeded, that checks may be skipped or that literal speed is the only useful response.
brief.boundaryZh: 趕在限時前完成，不等於事情已完成、必定失敗，或可以省略必要確認；要交代具體期限及任務。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把緊迫感當作成果保證，也不一定需要另一隊作競爭對手；時間有限，仍可分工核對關鍵資料。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述限時內的任務，分清時間壓力、實際行動及尚未知道的結果。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The rescue became a race against the clock.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 49, table 1, row 7; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: Restoring the captions became a race against the clock with the exhibition due to open in an hour; one person checked names while another placed labels, and the team counted what remained before deciding what could be ready.
listening.zh: 展覽一小時後就要開放，補回圖說成了一場與時間的競賽；一人核對姓名，另一人放置標籤，小組先點算仍有多少未完成，再決定哪些能趕及備妥。
listening.promptZh: 時間壓力來自甚麼？小組有沒有放棄核查？

options.en: The opening deadline created pressure, while name checks and a count still formed part of the work.
options.zh: 開放期限帶來壓力，但核對姓名及點算數量仍是工作的一部分。

options.en: The team had already restored every caption before the hour began.
options.zh: 這一小時開始前，小組已補回所有圖說。

options.en: The opening had been postponed by a day, leaving plenty of time to restore the labels.
options.zh: 展覽已延遲一天開放，所以有充裕時間補回標籤。

options.en: They decided that urgency removed the need to know which captions were missing.
options.zh: 小組決定，因為事情緊急，已不必知道缺少哪些圖說。

listening.explanationZh: 一小時後開放是限時壓力的來源；小組仍分工核姓名及未完成數量，不是全部已好、延期，或取消必要資訊。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼補回圖說變得緊迫？
reply.promptEn: Why did restoring the captions become urgent?

options.en: It became a race against the clock because the exhibition would open in an hour.
options.zh: 因為展覽一小時後就開放，這成了一場與時間的競賽。

options.en: The remaining captions had to be assessed against a close opening deadline.
options.zh: 餘下圖說需要按迫近的開放期限，判斷能否完成。

options.en: The team had little time to restore the labels and check what was still missing.
options.zh: 小組沒有多少時間補標籤及核對仍缺少甚麼。

options.en: The pressure came from the time left before visitors arrived, not a rival team.
options.zh: 壓力來自訪客到達前所剩的時間，而不是另一隊對手。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以迫近期限及餘下任務解釋緊迫感，不是在描述體育競賽。

scene.promptZh: 朋友寫完信，才得知當天郵件收集會在十分鐘後結束；她仍需核對地址並封好信，結果還不知道。哪句準確？

options.en: Getting the checked letter ready is a race against the clock, but we do not yet know whether it will reach that collection.
options.zh: 核對後把信備妥，是一場與時間的競賽，但我們還不知道她能否趕上這次收集。

options.en: The letter has already been collected, so no preparation remains.
options.zh: 信已被收走，所以沒有準備工作需要做。

options.en: The collection has already closed, so she is preparing the letter for the following day.
options.zh: 收集時間已過，所以她正在為翌日寄信作準備。

scene.explanationZh: 時間有限與結果未知可以並存；她仍有十分鐘及準備工作，不是已收走，也不是要等到翌日。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能從 a race against the clock 推論出來？

options.en: A task has strong time pressure.
options.zh: 任務帶有強烈的時間壓力。

options.en: The task is already successfully completed.
options.zh: 任務已經成功完成。

options.en: The exact deadline can explain the urgency.
options.zh: 具體期限可以解釋緊迫感。

contrast.explanationZh: 有時間壓力，不表示已有成功結果。

dialogue.promptZh: 同事問：「要趕開放時間，是否就不用核對姓名？」小組目前是一人核姓名，另一人放標籤。哪個回答最好？

options.en: It is a race against the clock, but the name check still matters; dividing the work lets us keep it in the process.
options.zh: 這是一場與時間的競賽，但核對姓名仍重要；分工讓我們保留這個步驟。

options.en: The deadline itself confirms that every name on the labels is correct.
options.zh: 期限本身就證明每張標籤上的姓名都正確。

options.en: All captions were finished earlier, so nobody is checking or placing labels now.
options.zh: 所有圖說早已完成，所以現在沒有人在核對或放標籤。

dialogue.explanationZh: 直接說明限時下仍需保留關鍵核查，不把緊急當作正確證據，也不否認正在做的工作。

speaking.en: It is a race against the clock, but I still need to know which checks are essential and what remains unfinished.
speaking.zh: 這是一場與時間的競賽，但我仍需要知道哪些核查不可省略，以及還有甚麼未完成。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清緊迫感與已知的結果。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你修改一段冒險小說旁白。人物原以為有整晚找信，後來才發現對方的船十分鐘後就開；你想先讓她問誰最後見過那封信，不立刻宣告已找到，也不責怪動作最慢的人。用兩句英文寫出實際旁白。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出可用的冒險旁白，交代時間突然縮短及先問線索的行動；保留信仍未找到的狀態，不以緊迫感代替證據或指責。

examples.en: Finding the letter had become a race against the clock: the boat would leave in ten minutes, not at dawn as she had thought. She asked who had seen it last before deciding where to begin the search.
examples.zh: 找信已成為一場與時間的競賽：船十分鐘後就開，不是她原以為的黎明。決定從哪裏開始找之前，她先問誰最後見過那封信。

examples.en: It was now a race against the clock, with the departure ten minutes away and the letter still missing. Instead of blaming the slowest helper, she asked for the last known sighting and divided the search from there.
examples.zh: 現在是一場與時間的競賽，距離開船只剩十分鐘，而信還未找到。她沒有責怪最慢的幫手，而是先問最後已知在哪裏見過信，再按線索分工尋找。

takeaways.en: Preparing the replacement programme was a race against the clock, and they marked the remaining gaps honestly.
takeaways.zh: 準備替換節目表成了一場與時間的競賽，他們仍如實標示尚未補齊的部分。

takeaways.en: The search became a race against the clock after the departure time changed, but the ending was still uncertain.
takeaways.zh: 出發時間改變後，尋找變成一場與時間的競賽，但結局仍未確定。

brief.meaningEn: Maintain a pace, level or continuing activity rather than let it drop.
brief.meaningZh: 維持某種步伐、水平或持續活動，不讓它下降或中斷。
brief.grammar: keep up the pace/a routine; keep it up; find it hard to keep up. This lesson teaches maintain + object or understood pace; keep up with names a comparison target in a related construction.
brief.register: Common maintenance phrasal verb. Continuing at a pace is different from increasing it, catching up from behind or already finishing the whole task.
brief.boundaryZh: 維持不等於加快、領先或完成所有工作；若想改為可承擔的節奏，應說清楚調整的是目標頻率。

listening.en: We had kept up a weekly reading bulletin for two months, but the editor would be away next week, so we discussed a substitute before promising the same pace; the past run did not tell us who would handle the next issue.
listening.zh: 我們已連續兩個月維持每周閱讀通訊，但編輯下周不在，所以在承諾維持同樣頻率前，先討論替補人選；過去持續出版，不表示下期已有人負責。
listening.promptZh: 過去已維持甚麼？下期仍需要安排甚麼？

options.en: The weekly run had continued for two months, while the next issue still needed an agreed substitute.
options.zh: 每周出版已持續兩個月，但下期仍需議定替補人選。

options.en: An agreed substitute will handle the next issue while the usual editor is away.
options.zh: 常任編輯不在時，下期會由已議定的替補人選處理。

options.en: The discussion concerned speeding delivery from weekly to daily.
options.zh: 討論內容是把每周出版加快為每日出版。

options.en: The bulletin had stopped after the first issue and had not appeared since.
options.zh: 通訊在首期後就停止，之後沒有再出版。

listening.explanationZh: 過去已維持每周出版，但下期人選仍需討論；不是已找好替補、改成每日，或只出版了一期。

reply.promptZh: 小組為甚麼在承諾出版下期前，先討論替補人選？
reply.promptEn: Why did the group discuss a substitute before promising the next issue?

options.en: We wanted to keep up the weekly bulletin while the usual editor was away.
options.zh: 我們想在常任編輯不在時，仍然維持每周通訊。

options.en: The next issue needed someone to handle it, despite the successful run so far.
options.zh: 雖然至今持續順利，下期仍需要有人處理。

options.en: Maintaining the same frequency required an arrangement beyond the person’s past work.
options.zh: 維持同樣頻率需要另作安排，不能只靠那人過去已完成的工作。

options.en: We had not yet agreed who could continue the publication during the absence.
options.zh: 我們還未議定，誰能在編輯缺席期間繼續出版。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋了維持頻率所需的未來安排；過去兩個月的成果，不是下期已有人負責的保證。

scene.promptZh: 學生打算每天畫一幅畫，但目前只做了一天，尚未安排其餘日子；你想分清打算與已持續做到的事。哪句最準確？

options.en: She wants to keep up a daily routine, but one day does not establish that she has maintained it over time.
options.zh: 她想維持每天畫畫的習慣，但做了一天，不足以證明已持續一段時間。

options.en: She has already maintained the daily drawing routine for several weeks.
options.zh: 她已連續幾周維持每天畫畫的習慣。

options.en: The account says she has already agreed to stop drawing altogether.
options.zh: 敘述說，她已同意完全停止畫畫。

scene.explanationZh: 目前只有一天的行動及往後意願；不能改寫成已連續幾周，也不能說她已放棄。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只從 keep up the pace 推論出來？

options.en: Maintain the stated rate.
options.zh: 維持所說的速度。

options.en: Increase the rate and finish every future task.
options.zh: 提高速度，並完成之後的每項任務。

options.en: Identify what will be needed to continue.
options.zh: 找出接下來繼續進行所需的條件。

contrast.explanationZh: 維持不等於加速，更不表示未來工作都已做完。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴問：「已連續出版兩個月，下周就不用再找人吧？」常任編輯下周不在。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Keeping up the bulletin still needs someone for the next issue; let us agree who can take that turn.
options.zh: 要維持通訊，下期仍需要有人負責；先議定誰能接這一輪吧。

options.en: Yes, the past issues already cover the editor’s future absence.
options.zh: 是的，過去幾期已經應付了編輯未來的缺席。

options.en: We should publish daily now, because keeping up means increasing the frequency.
options.zh: 現在應改成每日出版，因為 keep up 就是增加頻率。

dialogue.explanationZh: 持續出版需要接下來的安排；不能用過去成果代替未來人手，也不把維持誤解為加快。

speaking.en: I want to keep up the routine, but I need a plan I can actually continue rather than one successful day and an uncertain promise.
speaking.zh: 我想維持這個習慣，但需要一個實際上能持續的計劃，而不只是成功一天和一個不確定的承諾。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清一時做到與可以持續。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：搬離家人後，你原答應每天傳送很長的生活紀錄，雙方卻都感到負擔。你仍想保持聯絡，提議先每周一次較短但可持續的訊息，也想問家人喜歡的頻率，不把減量當作不關心。用一至兩句英文寫給家人。
writing.selfCheckZh: 提出可以協商的家庭聯絡安排，分清關心與可持續的頻率；先試再檢視，不把一次成功說成永久保證。

examples.en: I want to keep up our contact, but the long daily messages are more than I can promise honestly. Could we try one shorter update each week and ask after a month whether that rhythm works for us both?
examples.zh: 我想維持我們的聯絡，但每天的長訊息超出了我能誠實承諾的範圍。可否先試每周一則較短近況，一個月後再看這節奏是否適合我們雙方？

examples.en: Keeping up a regular exchange matters to me more than promising a daily report I cannot sustain. I would like a shorter weekly message for now, and I want to hear what frequency you would welcome too.
examples.zh: 對我而言，維持定期交流，比承諾自己無法持續的每日報告更重要。目前我想先用每周較短訊息，也想聽你希望多久聯絡一次。

takeaways.en: They kept up the weekly exchange by agreeing on a rota, rather than relying on one person every time.
takeaways.zh: 他們議定輪值來維持每周交流，而不是每次只依靠同一人。

takeaways.en: She wanted to keep up the practice, so she chose a frequency she could describe as a real commitment.
takeaways.zh: 她想維持練習，所以選了一個自己能認真承諾的頻率。

target.pattern: \bgiv(?:e|es|ing) (?:a|the) city a backbone\b|\bgave (?:a|the) city a backbone\b|\bgiven (?:a|the) city a backbone\b

brief.meaningEn: Provide a city with important underlying support or structure that other activities depend on.
brief.meaningZh: 為城市提供重要的基本支援或結構，讓其他活動得以依靠它進行。
brief.grammar: transport/a network gives a city a backbone; gave/has given the city a backbone. This give + object + support-image frame differs from describing a person’s courage or firmness.
brief.register: Productive structural-support metaphor. Identify the functions it supports; central support is not the only contributor and does not prove every district has equal access.
brief.boundaryZh: 支柱不等於唯一需要，也不表示服務已覆蓋全城；這裏不是說城市有真正骨骼，或形容市民的勇氣。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要用資料說明交通如何支持活動，不能只因稱它重要，就忽略仍未得到服務的人。
brief.outcomeZh: 能具體解釋基本網絡的支持作用，同時保留其他貢獻，以及尚未清楚的覆蓋範圍。

sources.sentence: Reliable transport gives a city a backbone.

listening.en: Residents said the reliable tram gave the city a backbone by linking homes, markets and workplaces throughout their day, though some outer streets still had no stop and the report did not claim that every journey was served.
listening.zh: 住戶說，可靠的電車把住處、市集和工作地點串連起來，支持他們一整天的活動，為城市提供支柱；但部分外圍街道仍沒有車站，報告也沒說每段旅程都得到服務。
listening.promptZh: 「支柱」體現在哪裏？服務覆蓋仍有甚麼限制？

options.en: The tram connected daily activities, while some outer streets still lacked a stop.
options.zh: 電車串連日常活動，但部分外圍街道仍沒有車站。

options.en: Every home already had a stop directly outside it.
options.zh: 每戶人家門外都已直接設有車站。

options.en: The service ran only for a special event and did not connect ordinary daily activities.
options.zh: 這服務只為特別活動運行，沒有串連普通日常活動。

options.en: The tram was proposed but had not yet carried any passengers.
options.zh: 電車仍是提案，尚未載過任何乘客。

listening.explanationZh: 實際串連日常用途，支持了結構支柱的意象，但外圍缺口仍在；不是每戶門前都有站、只供特別活動，或仍未投入服務。

reply.promptZh: 住戶為甚麼把電車視為城市的支柱？
reply.promptEn: Why did residents describe the tram as structural support for the city?

options.en: It gave the city a backbone by linking the places needed through an ordinary day.
options.zh: 它把普通一天所需的地方連起來，為城市提供支柱。

options.en: Homes, markets and workplaces were connected by a service residents relied on.
options.zh: 住處、市集及工作地點，由住戶依靠的交通服務串連。

options.en: The network supported several activities rather than one isolated journey.
options.zh: 這個網絡支持多種活動，而不是只有一段孤立的旅程。

options.en: Its importance came from the connections people used, not a claim that it reached every street.
options.zh: 它的重要性來自人們實際使用的連結，而不是聲稱它到達每條街。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以具體支持作用解釋重要性，不把核心地位當成全城已獲覆蓋。

scene.promptZh: 學生只畫好一條擬議路線，尚未建成或試行；他說它有望把分散的用途連起來，同伴卻說它已支持每天通行。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: The plan could give the city a backbone, but a route drawing alone does not show that the service is operating.
options.zh: 計劃有望為城市提供支柱，但路線圖本身不表示服務已經運作。

options.en: The drawing records a service already used every day by the residents.
options.zh: 這張圖記錄的是住戶已每日使用的服務。

options.en: The proposal has been rejected, so its possible connections are no longer being considered.
options.zh: 提案已被否決，所以不再考慮它可能提供的連結。

scene.explanationZh: 支持作用仍是提案的期望，圖上的路線不能證明服務已運作；資料也沒有說提案已被否決。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能從 give a city a backbone 的支持意象推論出來？

options.en: Provide a structure other activities depend on.
options.zh: 提供其他活動所依靠的結構。

options.en: Nothing else matters and every place is already served equally.
options.zh: 其他事物都不重要，而且每個地方都已獲同樣服務。

options.en: The explanation can show the links behind the judgement.
options.zh: 解釋可以指出支持這項判斷的實際連結。

contrast.explanationZh: 核心支持不是唯一貢獻，也不是全城同等覆蓋的證明。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友問：「電車既然是支柱，外圍街道沒有車站的問題就不用再問了嗎？」那些街道仍未接駁。哪個回應最好？

options.en: It has given the city a backbone, but that makes the remaining gaps worth identifying, not invisible.
options.zh: 它已為城市提供支柱，但這更讓餘下缺口值得找出來，而不是把它們變成看不見。

options.en: Its central role means the outer streets must already have stops, regardless of the map.
options.zh: 它的核心角色表示，無論地圖怎畫，外圍街道一定已有車站。

options.en: The missing stops prove that the existing connections have helped nobody.
options.zh: 仍有缺站的地方，證明現有連結沒有幫過任何人。

dialogue.explanationZh: 保留已提供的支持，也承認尚存的缺口，不用其中一面抹去另一面。

speaking.en: The network gives a city a backbone by supporting daily connections, though we should still ask which places remain outside it.
speaking.zh: 網絡透過支持日常連結，為城市提供支柱，但我們仍應問哪些地方還未納入其中。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再以實際支持解釋意象，同時承認仍有缺口。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為虛構城市歷史展寫前言。原稿只稱讚一位建線者，但訪問說明司機、維修者及乘客多年共同維持網絡可靠；你想把支柱意象連到持續共同工作，也保留仍缺接駁地區的聲音，不把一位英雄或一條線當作全城經驗。用一至兩句英文寫前言。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出可用的展覽前言，用持續共同工作支持支柱意象，並保留未接駁地區的聲音；不以單一英雄或開幕取代全城經驗。

examples.en: The tram gave the city a backbone through years of work by drivers, repairers and the people who used it. Their accounts belong here alongside the voices of districts still waiting for a connection, rather than behind a story of one person doing everything.
examples.zh: 電車透過司機、維修者及使用者多年的工作，為城市提供支柱。他們的敘述應在這裏，跟仍等接駁地區的聲音並列，而不是被一人包辦所有事的故事遮蓋。

examples.en: What gives a city a backbone is sustained through ordinary work as well as a celebrated opening. This exhibition follows those shared efforts and leaves room for people whose routes are still missing.
examples.zh: 為城市提供支柱的事物，不只靠一次受讚頌的開幕，也靠日常工作維持。這展覽追隨那些共同努力，並為仍缺路線的人留出空間。

glossary.en: drivers, repairers and the people who used it

glossary.zh: 他們的敘述應在這裏呈現

glossary.en: districts still waiting for a connection

takeaways.en: The reliable service gave the city a backbone, but its value depended on the people who kept the connections working.
takeaways.zh: 可靠的服務為城市提供支柱，但它的價值依靠那些持續維持連結的人。

takeaways.en: The proposal could give a city a backbone without answering every question about the areas it did not yet reach.
takeaways.zh: 提案可能為城市提供支柱，但這不表示它已回答未覆蓋地區的每個問題。

titleEn: paint all overseas cities with the same brush

target.pattern: \bpaint(?:s|ed|ing)? (?:all overseas cities|all (?:the )?cities|them all) with the same brush\b

brief.meaningEn: Treat different cities as if they shared the same relevant characteristics, using a broad painting comparison.
brief.meaningZh: 用「同一畫筆」作比較，把不同城市當作具有相同的相關特點。
brief.grammar: paint all overseas cities with the same brush; painted/painting. In this supplied creative wording the focus is an unsupported blanket assumption; identify the feature being generalised.
brief.register: Contextual painting comparison, taught with the guide’s broad identical-treatment meaning. The established tar everyone with the same brush idiom specifically involves unfair negative generalisation and should not silently replace this broader source frame.
brief.boundaryZh: 一概而論也可以涉及中性的實際安排，不一定是在貶低地方；要指出忽略了哪項差異，不能只因都是海外城市就當作相同。
brief.misconceptionZh: 兩個地方有相似之處，不表示所有安排都一樣；需要查問差異，也不表示已預定哪個地方更好。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出缺乏根據的一概假設，並以當地的具體資訊修正，而不添加不必要的負面標籤。

listening.zh: 規劃晚間參觀時，我曾把所有海外城市一概看成相同，以為開放時間都一樣；兩個場地的不同告示，令我改為查看當地資訊，而不是到哪裏都套用同一張時間表。

options.en: The speaker assumed identical opening times, then used local notices to check each visit.
options.zh: 說話者原以為開放時間相同，後來才按當地告示核對每次參觀的安排。

options.en: The speaker had compared every venue before forming the original timetable.

options.en: The two venues displayed the same opening hours, confirming the original plan.
options.zh: 兩個場地顯示相同的開放時間，確認原計劃沒有問題。

options.en: The speaker used another city’s timetable for the next visit without checking that venue.
options.zh: 說話者沒有查看下一個場地，就把另一城市的時間表直接套用。

listening.explanationZh: 需要修正的是開放時間相同的假設；後來改為查當地資訊，不是已做全面比較、證明時段相同，或繼續套用別城安排。

reply.promptZh: 說話者為甚麼不再把同一時間表套用到不同城市？
reply.promptEn: Why did the speaker stop reusing one timetable across cities?

options.en: I had painted all overseas cities with the same brush, but the different notices showed that my opening-time assumption did not hold.
options.zh: 我曾把所有海外城市看成相同，但不同告示顯示，我對開放時間的假設並不成立。

options.en: The venues did not share the identical hours I had expected.
options.zh: 場地的開放時間並不像我原先以為的那樣完全相同。

options.en: Local information gave me a reason to check rather than reuse the old timetable.
options.zh: 當地資料令我有理由重新核對，而不是繼續用舊時間表。

options.en: The difference concerned practical visiting arrangements, not a judgement that one place was better.
options.zh: 這項差異涉及實際參觀安排，不是要判哪個地方比較好。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都回應了實際時段差異；修正原先假設，不等於貶低某個地方。

scene.promptZh: 兩個城市的展覽都在河邊，但其中一個需要預約，另一個可以直接到場；朋友只因位置相似，就以為入場方法相同。哪句最好？

options.en: We should not paint all cities with the same brush; the riverside setting does not settle their booking arrangements.
options.zh: 不應把所有城市一概看成相同；同在河邊，不能決定兩者的預約安排。

options.en: The similar location confirms that neither exhibition requires any booking.
options.zh: 位置相似就證明，兩個展覽都不需要預約。

options.en: The account says both organisers have agreed to use one shared entry rule.
options.zh: 敘述說，兩個主辦者已同意採用同一套入場規則。

scene.explanationZh: 相似位置不代表入場安排相同；資料已明說一個需預約，另一個可直接到場。

contrast.promptZh: 單憑兩個城市都屬海外，最不能推論哪一項？

options.en: Their opening and entry arrangements are identical in every relevant respect.
options.zh: 它們的開放及入場安排，在每個相關方面都完全相同。

options.en: Local information may be needed to plan a visit.
options.zh: 計劃參觀時，可能需要查看當地資訊。

options.en: A similarity should be separated from unexamined differences.
options.zh: 應把已知相似處，跟尚未查過的差異分開。

contrast.explanationZh: 「海外」只是一種分類，不是實際安排完全相同的證據。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友問：「兩個展覽都在河邊，我照上次的預約方法就行吧？」其中一個需預約，另一個可直接到場。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Let us not paint all cities with the same brush; check this exhibition’s entry notice rather than infer it from the riverside location.
options.zh: 別把所有城市一概看成相同；先查這個展覽的入場告示，不要只憑河邊位置推斷。

options.en: Yes, the shared location means both exhibitions use the same booking system.
options.zh: 可以，位置相似表示兩個展覽採用同一套預約系統。

options.en: The two organisers have already given us one joint confirmation, so no separate rule applies.
options.zh: 兩個主辦者已給我們共同確認，所以沒有個別規則需要看。

dialogue.explanationZh: 按這次展覽的實際資訊回應，不由位置推斷制度，也不自行加上共同確認。

speaking.en: I do not want to paint all overseas cities with the same brush, so I will check the local arrangements without deciding in advance which place is better.
speaking.zh: 我不想把所有海外城市一概看成相同，所以會查當地安排，不預先判定哪個地方比較好。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清一概假設與有根據的具體比較。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你編一本虛構旅行人物的筆記。她把一個城市的河邊早餐，寫成「海外城市都這樣開始一天」；她只親歷一城，還沒到另一城。你想保留她喜歡的早餐描寫，但把未去地方的情況留作問題，不寫成已知規則。用一至兩句英文給她回饋。
writing.selfCheckZh: 保留具體的親身描寫，修正對未到過城市的普遍化；不預定所有城市都相同，也不加上原文沒有的負面特質。

examples.en: The breakfast scene is worth keeping, but let us not paint all overseas cities with the same brush from this one visit. Could you name the city and your own morning, then leave the next place as something still to discover?
examples.zh: 早餐場景值得保留，但別憑這次參觀，就把所有海外城市一概看成相同。可否寫清是哪個城市、你自己的早晨，再把下一個地方留待探索？

examples.en: You can keep the riverside breakfast without painting all cities with the same brush. I would frame it as the morning you experienced, not a rule about places the character has not yet visited.
examples.zh: 你可以保留河邊早餐，而不必把所有城市一概看成相同。我會把它寫成你親歷的早晨，而不是人物尚未到過的地方都遵循的規則。

takeaways.en: She had painted all overseas cities with the same brush until local questions made her reconsider the timetable.
takeaways.zh: 她曾把所有海外城市一概看成相同，直到當地的問題令她重新考慮時間表。

takeaways.en: We need not paint all cities with the same brush when the details already show different ways of using the same kind of space.
takeaways.zh: 細節已顯示同類空間有不同用法時，我們不必把所有城市一概看成相同。

titleZh: 在地圖上畫線、標示路線

target.pattern: \bdraw(?:s|ing)? lines on a map\b|\bdrew lines on a map\b|\bdrawn lines on a map\b

brief.meaningEn: Representing routes or boundaries in a simplified plan, especially when contrasted with the human experience that the plan alone does not capture.
brief.meaningZh: 在簡化的規劃中標示路線或界線，尤其用來對比圖面本身沒有呈現的實際生活。
brief.grammar: planning involves more than drawing lines on a map; draw/drew/drawn. Drawing can be literal, while the wider contrast criticises treating the drawing as a complete account.
brief.register: Contextual concrete image used in planning criticism. More than does not mean maps are useless; people’s actual journeys, needs and accounts may add what a line cannot show.
brief.boundaryZh: 這不是否定地圖，也不表示畫了線就已能通行或獲人同意；還需要了解實際使用情況及生活經驗。
brief.misconceptionZh: 一條連線不能說明所有通行時間及個人感受；反過來，訪問也不能取代所有位置資訊。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分清圖上的表示與生活中的實現，提出具體需要補充的資訊，不把選擇簡化為完全靠地圖或完全不用。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Urban planning involves more than drawing lines on a map.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 50, table 1, row 2; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: Planning the route was more than drawing lines on a map: the shortest line crossed a gate locked in the evenings, so the group asked the caretaker about access before describing the walk to visitors.
listening.zh: 規劃路線不只是在地圖上畫線：最短路線穿過一道晚間上鎖的門，所以小組先問管理員通行安排，再向訪客介紹這段步行路線。
listening.promptZh: 圖上的連線漏了甚麼？小組先向誰查問？

options.en: The gate’s evening access affected the route, so the caretaker was asked before visitors were advised.
options.zh: 門的晚間開放情況影響路線，所以小組向訪客提出建議前，先問管理員。

options.en: The shortest drawn line had already been confirmed open at every time.
options.zh: 畫出的最短路線已確認，在任何時段都能通行。

options.en: The group discarded the map and decided no location information was useful.
options.zh: 小組丟掉地圖，認為所有位置資訊都沒有用。

options.en: The gate had been removed before anyone considered the route.
options.zh: 在任何人考慮路線之前，那道門就已被拆除。

listening.explanationZh: 地圖仍提供位置資訊，但需要補上門的晚間情況；不能由連線推斷全時開放，也未說門已拆除。

reply.promptZh: 小組為甚麼不直接向訪客推薦圖上最短的路線？
reply.promptEn: Why did the group not simply recommend the shortest drawn line?

options.en: Planning meant more than drawing lines on a map because the evening gate could interrupt the actual walk.
options.zh: 晚間上鎖的門可能阻斷實際步行，所以規劃不只是在地圖上畫線。

options.en: The drawn connection did not establish whether visitors could pass through at the needed time.
options.zh: 圖上的連接，沒有確認訪客在所需時段能否通過。

options.en: The caretaker’s information was needed to understand how the route worked in practice.
options.zh: 需要管理員提供資訊，才能了解路線實際怎樣使用。

options.en: A short distance on paper was not enough to confirm usable access.
options.zh: 紙上距離短，不足以確認真的能夠通行。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋了圖上連線與實際通行之間的資訊缺口，而不是說地圖完全無用。

scene.promptZh: 兩區之間的步道已開放，地圖也畫出連接，但還沒問過住戶之間的交流；學生卻說，有連線就證明兩區的人都相熟。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: Drawing lines on a map can show the route, but we still need residents’ accounts before describing their relationships.
options.zh: 在地圖上畫線可以顯示路線，但描述居民關係前，仍需要聽他們的經驗。

options.en: The opened path records residents explaining the friendships it has already created.
options.zh: 已開放的步道，記錄了居民對它已創造的友誼所作的解釋。

options.en: The map contains the households’ social contacts rather than the position of the path.
options.zh: 地圖記載的是各戶的社交聯絡，而不是步道位置。

scene.explanationZh: 實際路線可以連接空間，但人際關係仍需另有資料；地圖及開通步道，不等於已做訪問或取得社交紀錄。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合「規劃不只是在地圖上畫線」的提醒？

options.en: Use the drawing and investigate what happens along the route.
options.zh: 使用圖面，同時了解路線上的實際情況。

options.en: Assume a marked connection proves access at every needed time.
options.zh: 假定標示出的連接，已證明每個需要的時段都可以通行。

options.en: Distinguish represented space from how people can use it.
options.zh: 分清圖上呈現的空間，以及人們實際能如何使用。

contrast.explanationZh: 連線是一種表示，不是所有時段均能通行的證明。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友問：「地圖已連到目的地，就不用再問門的晚間情況吧？」那道門夜間會上鎖。哪個回應最好？

options.en: The route needs more than drawing lines on a map; let us ask when the gate is usable before recommending it.
options.zh: 規劃路線不只是在地圖上畫線；推薦之前，先問清楚門在哪些時段可以通過。

options.en: Yes, the drawn line overrides the gate’s actual opening conditions.
options.zh: 是的，圖上的連線可以取代門的實際開放條件。

options.en: We should recommend a longer route solely because it looks less direct on paper.
options.zh: 我們應只因另一條路在紙上看來較迂迴，就推薦那條較長路線。

dialogue.explanationZh: 保留地圖與實況的互補作用，先查通行條件；不能由連線推斷開放，也不只憑線條是否迂迴作推薦。

speaking.en: Drawing lines on a map can help us begin, but we still need to ask how people use those connections in real situations.
speaking.zh: 在地圖上畫線可以幫我們起步，但仍需要了解人們在實際情況中怎樣使用那些連接。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清圖面表示與實際使用。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為學生城市展設計訪客提問卡。地圖上有一條新步道，但還沒有附近居民對安全感、停留或照顧家人路程的經驗；你想邀請大家補充自己的使用情況，不預定人人支持或反對。用兩句英文寫出可直接放在卡上的邀請。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出可直接使用的邀請卡內容，詢問個人生活經驗，並保留不同意的空間；讓參與者補充圖面未呈現的需要，不預定支持結論。

examples.en: Drawing lines on a map tells us where this path is proposed, but not what it would mean in your day. Tell us about a journey, a place to pause or a caring responsibility that you would want the plan to consider.
examples.zh: 在地圖上畫線，告訴我們步道擬議的位置，卻沒有說它對你一天的生活有何意義。請分享一段路程、一處想停留的地方，或一項你希望計劃考慮的照顧責任。

examples.en: We want to go beyond drawing lines on a map by hearing how people might use the space. Your experience may add a need or a question we have missed; you do not have to agree with the proposal to contribute.
examples.zh: 我們想聽人們可能怎樣使用空間，讓討論超越地圖上的連線。你的經驗也許能補充我們漏掉的需要或問題；你不必同意提案，也可以作出貢獻。

glossary.en: a need or a question we have missed
glossary.zh: 我們遺漏的需要或問題

takeaways.en: The discussion moved beyond drawing lines on a map when residents explained the journeys hidden behind the proposed route.
takeaways.zh: 居民說明擬議路線背後的日常旅程後，討論便不再只停留於地圖上的連線。

takeaways.en: Drawing lines on a map showed possible links, while the interviews revealed which everyday needs still required attention.
takeaways.zh: 地圖上的連線顯示可能的連接，訪問則揭示哪些日常需要仍待關注。

titleZh: 樓宇間難辨方向的迷宮

brief.meaningEn: A built environment experienced as confusing to navigate, using a maze image for its routes and structures.
brief.meaningZh: 把路線及建築結構令人難辨方向的建成環境，比作迷宮。
brief.grammar: a district feels like/becomes a concrete maze; find one’s way through the concrete maze. The image describes navigation or perceived complexity, not literal game walls or every resident’s experience.
brief.register: Productive urban metaphor. Identify the layout or viewpoint behind the confusion; unfamiliarity may contribute, and the image does not show that residents intend to trap anyone.
brief.boundaryZh: 難以辨路不等於真的被囚、沒有出口，或所有人都不友善；也不能只因使用混凝土建築，就判定人一定會迷路。
brief.misconceptionZh: 清楚地標或熟路者可能提供幫助；不要把一位初訪者的感受，變成全區每個人都迷失。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體路線及人物視角支持迷宮意象，保留尚未知的原因，以及其他人的不同經驗。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Poor planning turned the district into a concrete maze.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 50, table 1, row 3; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: On my first visit, the estate felt like a concrete maze: similar entrances faced different courtyards and hid the street, while a resident knew the layout and showed me a marked route.
listening.zh: 第一次到訪時，我覺得屋苑像一座混凝土迷宮：相似入口朝向不同庭院，也擋住了街道視野；一位住戶卻熟悉布局，指給我看一條有標記的路線。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼讓初訪者困惑？住戶的經驗有何不同？

options.en: Repeated entrances and a limited view confused the newcomer, while a resident could identify a route.
options.zh: 重複入口及受限視野令初訪者混亂，但住戶能辨認一條路線。

options.en: The confusion came from contradictory directions given by the resident, rather than the entrances and view.
options.zh: 困惑來自住戶給的矛盾方向，而不是入口及視野。

options.en: The resident had no idea where any marked route led.
options.zh: 住戶不知道任何有標記的路線通往哪裏。

options.en: The visitor was describing a route used every day rather than an unfamiliar first visit.
options.zh: 訪客描述的是每天使用的路線，而不是一次陌生的初訪。

listening.explanationZh: 初訪者難辨方向與熟路者能指路可以並存；不能改成住戶給錯方向，或訪客早已天天走這條路。

reply.promptZh: 初訪者為甚麼把屋苑比作迷宮？
reply.promptEn: Why did the newcomer compare the estate to a maze?

options.en: It felt like a concrete maze because the similar entrances and hidden street made orientation difficult.
options.zh: 相似入口及被遮住的街道，令我難以辨認方向，所以屋苑感覺像混凝土迷宮。

options.en: I could not distinguish the courtyard approaches easily from where I stood.
options.zh: 從我站的位置，很難分清通往不同庭院的入口。

options.en: The repeated built forms made it hard for me to relate the entrances to the street.
options.zh: 重複的建築形式，令我難以把各入口和街道位置連起來。

options.en: My view lacked the landmarks that the resident already knew how to use.
options.zh: 我看到的景象缺少那些住戶已懂得運用的地標。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以具體布局及視角解釋困惑，沒有把初訪者的感受當作居民意圖的證據。

scene.promptZh: 另一區樓宇用料相同，但入口各有清楚標記，訪客說按圖能順利找到；你卻只因混凝土建築多，就稱它為迷宮。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: Concrete alone does not make it a concrete maze when the described routes are clear to the visitors.
options.zh: 既然訪客認為所述路線清楚，單是混凝土建築，不會使它成為難辨方向的迷宮。

options.en: The account says the signs were identical and the visitors could not find any entrance.
options.zh: 敘述說，各標記完全相同，訪客找不到任何入口。

options.en: The visitors’ successful route confirms that no directions were present.
options.zh: 訪客成功找到路，證明現場沒有任何指示。

scene.explanationZh: 迷宮意象需要難辨方向的根據，不能只靠建築材料；也不能把有指示而順利找到路的情況寫成相反。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能從 a concrete maze 的城市意象推論出來？

options.en: The layout is experienced as confusing to navigate.
options.zh: 當事人覺得布局令人難以辨路。

options.en: Residents deliberately designed a trap for the visitor.
options.zh: 居民故意為訪客設下陷阱。

options.en: A different viewpoint or local knowledge may change the experience.
options.zh: 不同視角或當地知識可能改變體驗。

contrast.explanationZh: 導航上的混亂，不是居民有惡意或故意設計陷阱的證據。

dialogue.promptZh: 住戶問：「你稱這裏為迷宮，是說我們故意不讓你出去嗎？」他剛替你指路。哪個回答最好？

options.en: No, I meant that the layout felt like a concrete maze to me; your directions helped me understand it.
options.zh: 不是，我是說這個布局對我而言像混凝土迷宮；你的指路幫我理解了它。

options.en: Yes, my first confusion is enough to know that you intended to trap me.
options.zh: 是的，我初到時的困惑，已足以讓我知道你想把我困住。

options.en: I never had trouble with the entrances, so there was no reason to ask for directions.
options.zh: 我從來沒有難辨入口，所以沒有理由向人問路。

dialogue.explanationZh: 直接澄清自己的視角，並感謝實際幫助；不以困惑推斷惡意，也不否認自己曾遇到困難。

speaking.en: The place seemed like a concrete maze from my first viewpoint, but a resident’s directions helped me find the route.
speaking.zh: 從我初到時的視角看，這地方像混凝土迷宮，但住戶的指路幫我找到路線。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再保留個人視角及實際得到的幫助。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在社區通訊寫自己初到時找不到入口，原稿用迷宮意象後，卻加上「大家都想把外人擋住」。幫你找路的住戶說那句話令人受傷；你想道歉，保留自己的困惑，但撤回對所有人意圖的指控，並感謝她的幫助。用一至兩句英文回覆。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出實際道歉，把自己的導航困惑與沒有證據的居民意圖分開；感謝具體幫助並承諾修正，不用強烈比喻代替指控的根據。

examples.en: I am sorry I turned my experience of a concrete maze into a claim about everyone’s intentions. I meant that I could not read the layout at first, and I should have included how your help made the route clearer.
examples.zh: 對不起，我把自己置身混凝土迷宮的感受，變成對所有人意圖的指控。我原想說，起初看不懂布局，也應該寫上你的幫助如何讓路線變清楚。

examples.en: Calling the estate a concrete maze described my confusion, but saying people wanted to keep outsiders away went beyond what I knew. Thank you for showing me the route; I will correct that unfair assumption.
examples.zh: 把屋苑稱為混凝土迷宮，是在描述我的困惑；但說大家想擋住外人，已超出了我知道的事。謝謝你替我指路，我會改正這個不公平的假設。

glossary.en: your help made the route clearer
glossary.zh: 你的幫助讓路線更清楚
改正那個不公平的假設

takeaways.en: The repeated entrances made the estate feel like a concrete maze to the visitor until someone explained the signs.
takeaways.zh: 重複的入口令訪客覺得屋苑像混凝土迷宮，直到有人解釋那些標記。

takeaways.en: A concrete maze was how she described the confusing layout, not a verdict on the neighbours who helped her.
takeaways.zh: 「混凝土迷宮」是她對難辨布局的形容，不是對曾幫助她的鄰居所作的評斷。

titleZh: 只求存放人的機械式城市

brief.meaningEn: A critical image of a place treating residents as units to be accommodated rather than people with active lives and needs.
brief.meaningZh: 以批評性的意象形容一個地方，只把居民當作需要安置的單位，而不是有自己生活及需要的人。
brief.grammar: a city should not become a machine for storing people. Storing supplies a passive container image; explain what human experience is missing from the account.
brief.register: Creative critical machine/container metaphor. The target of criticism is the way a place is designed or represented, not the worth of its residents or a claim that all people are passive.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是把居民真的當成物件，也不是否定提供住所；要指出忽略了哪些生活或人物行動，不以容量一項取代所有人的需要。
brief.misconceptionZh: 批評只顧存放人，不表示居民本身沒有感情及意願，也不是要求取消必要住所。
brief.outcomeZh: 能解釋這個存放意象所批評的視角，同時保留人的主動性及實際住房需要。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A city should never become a machine for storing people.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 50, table 1, row 5; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The novel’s opening made the city seem like a machine for storing people, listing room numbers but giving residents no names or actions; the reviewer wanted later scenes to reveal their choices, not simply more space statistics.
listening.zh: 小說開頭只列房間號碼，沒有寫居民的名字或行動，令城市像一部存放人的機器；評論者想在後面的場景看見居民的選擇，而不只是更多空間統計。
listening.promptZh: 評論者批評甚麼？希望增加哪些內容？

options.en: The opening reduced residents to accommodation details, so the reviewer wanted their choices shown.
options.zh: 開頭把居民縮減為安置細節，所以評論者想看見他們的選擇。

options.en: The reviewer said residents themselves had no feelings or ability to act.
options.zh: 評論者認為居民本身沒有感情，也沒有行動能力。

options.en: The opening already followed named residents making choices throughout the chapter.
options.zh: 開頭整章都已跟隨具名居民作出不同選擇。

options.en: The request was for a larger table of room sizes instead of any character scene.
options.zh: 評論者要求更大的房間尺寸表，而不要任何人物場景。

listening.explanationZh: 批評針對敘事中缺少人物的生活，想加入行動及選擇；不是貶低居民，也不是只要求更多數據。

reply.promptZh: 評論者為甚麼覺得開頭像只在存放人的系統？
reply.promptEn: Why did the reviewer see the opening as an impersonal accommodation system?

options.en: It resembled a machine for storing people because room numbers replaced residents’ names and actions.
options.zh: 房間號碼取代了居民的名字及行動，所以它像一部存放人的機器。

options.en: The description told us where people were placed without showing what they chose to do.
options.zh: 描述只告訴我們人被安置在哪裏，沒有呈現他們選擇做甚麼。

options.en: Accommodation details dominated the opening while human experiences were absent.
options.zh: 安置細節主導開頭，人的經驗卻沒有出現。

options.en: The reviewer had no character decisions to follow in the listed rooms.
options.zh: 評論者在那些列出的房間中，找不到可以跟隨的人物決定。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出敘事缺少人物行動的根據，沒有說居民本身缺乏價值。

scene.promptZh: 圖畫小說先用整齊門牌呈現冷感，後頁卻跟隨不同住戶種花、商量作息，以及拒絕不想參加的活動；有人只看首圖，就稱人物毫無主動性。哪句最好？

options.en: The first image may suggest a machine for storing people, but the later actions give the residents choices and voices.
options.zh: 首圖也許讓人想到存放人的機器，但後面的行動讓居民有選擇及聲音。

options.en: The later actions are only promises about future scenes, rather than events actually shown.
options.zh: 後面的行動只是對未來場景的承諾，不是實際已呈現的事件。

options.en: The account says the later pages contain only larger room-number diagrams.
options.zh: 敘述說，後面幾頁只有更大的房號圖。

scene.explanationZh: 需要閱讀後頁已呈現的行動，不能讓首圖意象蓋過其後的人物，也不能把後頁內容說成只是承諾。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 a machine for storing people 的批評方向？

options.en: Question whether planning or description leaves out residents’ active lives.
options.zh: 追問規劃或描述是否忽略了居民的主動生活。

options.en: Declare that the people themselves are worthless objects.
options.zh: 宣稱人本身是沒有價值的物件。

options.en: Explain what experience or choice would add the missing human dimension.
options.zh: 解釋哪種經驗或選擇能補上缺失的人的面向。

contrast.explanationZh: 批評的是設計或敘事的視角，不是貶低人的價值。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友問：「你說存放人的機器，是說住戶都沒有感情嗎？」你批評的其實是小說只列房間號碼。哪個回答最好？

options.en: No, a machine for storing people describes the opening’s narrow view; I want the residents’ feelings and choices to become visible.
options.zh: 不是，存放人的機器是在形容開頭狹窄的視角；我想讓居民的感受及選擇被看見。

options.en: Yes, the room numbers prove the residents have no inner lives.
options.zh: 是的，房間號碼證明居民沒有內心生活。

options.en: I am asking for the housing to disappear, rather than for the story to show its people.
options.zh: 我是在要求住房消失，而不是要求故事呈現住在那裏的人。

dialogue.explanationZh: 評論針對敘事視角，並要求補上人物；不能把它改成對內心的定論，或取消住所的要求。

speaking.en: The opening feels like a machine for storing people, so I want to know how the residents choose, connect and give the place meaning.
speaking.zh: 開頭感覺像一部存放人的機器，所以我想了解居民怎樣選擇、連繫彼此，以及為地方賦予意義。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清對視角的批評與居民本身的主動性。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫未來城市劇的一段住戶對白。管理者只問她需要多少房間，她卻想說住所重要，但自己也需要選擇何時見人、保留安靜，以及照顧植物。用一至兩句英文寫她實際說的話，不把生活需要寫成拒絕住所，也不代表所有住戶發言。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出住戶可說的完整對白，以具體的自主日常表達生活需要；保留住房的價值及自己發言的範圍，不貶低居民，也不替所有人作決定。

examples.en: I need a home, but I do not want this city to become a machine for storing people. Ask me when I want company, when I need quiet and where I can care for a few plants, rather than only how many rooms will hold me.
examples.zh: 我需要一個家，但不想這城市變成一部存放人的機器。除了問多少房間能容納我，也請問我何時想有人陪、何時需要安靜，以及在哪裏可以照顧幾盆植物。

examples.en: A machine for storing people would leave no place for the choices that make this a home for me. I want somewhere to live and some say in the ordinary things I do there, without claiming to speak for every neighbour.
examples.zh: 存放人的機器，不會為那些讓這裏成為我家的選擇留出空間。我想有地方住，也想對自己在那裏的日常事情有些發言權，但不聲稱代表每位鄰居。

glossary.en: some say in the ordinary things
glossary.zh: 對日常事情有些發言權

takeaways.en: The narrator rejected a machine for storing people and began to show the choices made behind the numbered doors.
takeaways.zh: 敘述者拒絕把城市只看成存放人的機器，開始呈現編號門後那些人作出的選擇。

takeaways.en: A city need not become a machine for storing people when its residents have a voice in how daily spaces are used.
takeaways.zh: 居民能對日常空間怎樣使用發聲時，城市不必成為一部存放人的機器。

target.pattern: \bgiv(?:e|es|ing) away clues\b|\bgave away clues\b|\bgiven away clues\b

brief.meaningEn: Reveal hints that let others infer something, often without intending to disclose it.
brief.meaningZh: 透露讓別人能作推測的提示，而這種透露往往不是有意的。
brief.grammar: details give away clues about/to something; gave/has given away clues. Give away is the revealing unit; clues are partial indications, not automatically a complete or uniquely certain explanation.
brief.register: Common reveal-hint construction. Unintentional revelation fits the supplied accent example, but an author can also deliberately reveal clues. A speech feature alone does not establish someone’s whole history or identity.
brief.boundaryZh: 線索不是全貌，也不一定只有一個解釋；聲音特徵可來自多種經驗，不能單憑一句話斷定背景或能力。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把推測當作已證實的事，也不把所有透露都視為有意；需要看具體線索及其他可能解釋。
brief.outcomeZh: 能表達細節只提供提示，而非完整答案，並分清觀察、推測及仍需查問的資訊。

sources.sentence: Her accent gives away clues about where she grew up.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 50, table 2, row 3; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The character’s careful folding gave away clues about an earlier job: she made the same precise crease without thinking, but the reader still needed another scene before knowing where she had learned it.
listening.zh: 角色小心摺疊的動作，透露了以前工作的線索：她不假思索地摺出同樣精確的摺痕，但讀者仍需要看另一個場景，才知道她在哪裏學會。
listening.promptZh: 這個細節透露了多少資訊？

options.en: A practised action suggested a background connection without yet identifying its source.
options.zh: 熟練動作暗示與過去背景有關，但尚未指明來源。

options.en: The action confirms that she currently works at the place where this scene is set.
options.zh: 動作確認她目前就在這個場景的地點工作。

options.en: The fold is a new skill she is trying for the first time in this scene.
options.zh: 這個摺法是她在本場景第一次嘗試的新技能。

options.en: The reader had already watched the training scene before the fold appeared.
options.zh: 摺疊動作出現之前，讀者已看過她受訓的場景。

listening.explanationZh: 不經意而熟練的動作提供部分提示，但來源仍未揭示；不是完整履歷，也不是讀者先前已知道的背景。

reply.promptZh: 作者為甚麼先寫摺疊習慣，之後才解釋背景？
reply.promptEn: Why did the author show the folding habit before explaining its background?

options.en: It gave away clues about an earlier part of her life without explaining the whole history at once.
options.zh: 它透露她較早人生經歷的線索，卻沒有一次交代整段歷史。

options.en: The repeated precision suggested an experience the reader had not yet seen.
options.zh: 反覆而準確的動作，暗示讀者還未見過的經驗。

options.en: The action could make readers ask where she had learned it.
options.zh: 這個動作能讓讀者想問，她是在哪裏學會的。

options.en: A small physical habit hinted at a past connection before the later scene supplied context.
options.zh: 後面的場景補充背景之前，一個小小的身體習慣先暗示了過去的連結。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都回應了先提示、後交代背景的敘事作用，不把線索當作一切已知。

scene.promptZh: 讀者看見角色留下一個車站號碼，就猜她的職業，但小說尚未解釋，仍有多種可能。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: The number may give away clues, but it does not by itself establish her occupation.
options.zh: 號碼可能透露線索，但本身不能確定她的職業。

options.en: The station number confirms that she currently works there rather than visiting for another reason.
options.zh: 車站號碼確認她目前在那裏工作，而不是因其他理由到訪。

options.en: The current scene states her occupation directly rather than leaving the number unexplained.
options.zh: 目前場景已直接交代她的職業，並沒有把號碼留待解釋。

scene.explanationZh: 提示與已確定的身份要分清；在後文未交代前，不應當作已經得到解釋。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能從 give away clues 推論出來？

options.en: Some detail reveals a hint.
options.zh: 某個細節透露了一點提示。

options.en: The hint supplies a complete, unique explanation without further context.
options.zh: 提示不需其他背景，就能提供完整而唯一的解釋。

options.en: The revealing can be unintended, while an author may also place it deliberately.
options.zh: 人物可能無意透露，而作者也可能有意安排線索。

contrast.explanationZh: 線索本身不保證完整或唯一的答案。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友問：「只看到摺法，我就能斷定她在哪裏工作嗎？」背景尚未揭示。哪個回應最好？

options.en: It gives away clues, but let us keep that as a possibility until the story supplies more context.
options.zh: 它透露了線索，但故事補充更多背景前，先把這視為一種可能吧。

options.en: Yes, the single fold confirms the employer without any other scene.
options.zh: 可以，單一摺法已能確認僱主，不用再看其他場景。

options.en: She has already explained her entire career to us, so the clue adds no uncertainty.
options.zh: 她已向我們解釋整段職業生涯，所以這線索沒有留下任何不確定。

dialogue.explanationZh: 自然地保留部分推測，不把它說成已取得完整背景。

speaking.en: The detail gives away clues about her past, but I want more context before choosing one explanation.
speaking.zh: 這細節透露她過去的線索，但選定一個解釋前，我想先得到更多背景。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清提示、推測與確認。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替朋友編家庭照片小冊，照片角落有信封和地址字跡。她只同意分享聚會，不想讓讀者推測住處；你想提醒她，小細節可能透露線索，再問她想保留、裁掉還是遮去，不擅自決定。用一至兩句英文寫實際訊息。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出尊重本人選擇的提醒，說明可能透露線索，而不是已知完整住址；詢問保留、裁掉或遮去的意願，不用分享照片的同意取代所有細節的同意。

examples.en: The envelope in the corner could give away clues about where you live, even though the photograph is meant to show the gathering. Would you like to keep that detail, crop it out or cover the writing before we share the booklet?
examples.zh: 角落的信封可能透露你住處的線索，即使照片本來只是想呈現聚會。分享小冊前，你想保留這細節、裁掉它，還是遮去字跡？

examples.en: Small background details can give away clues that you did not mean to share. Could we look at the envelope together and decide what you are comfortable including, rather than assume your agreement to the gathering photograph covers everything in it?
examples.zh: 小小的背景細節，可能透露你無意分享的線索。可否一起看看信封，決定你願意包括甚麼，而不假定你同意分享聚會照片，就包括裏面的所有內容？

takeaways.en: The handwriting gave away clues about a shared habit, though the narrator waited before naming the connection.
takeaways.zh: 字跡透露一個共同習慣的線索，但敘述者到稍後才說明兩者的連結。

takeaways.en: Small details can give away clues without telling us everything about the person behind them.
takeaways.zh: 細小的內容可以透露線索，卻不等於告訴我們背後人物的一切。

brief.meaningEn: Give a rough general shape or broad account, without supplying all the details.
brief.meaningZh: 提供一個粗略的整體形態或概況，不交代全部細節。
brief.grammar: sketch the outline of a plan/story/experience; sketched/sketching. The drawing image can describe spoken or written explanation, not necessarily pencil marks.
brief.register: Common outline-description frame. A broad account can be useful, but it does not establish that every detail is decided, accurate or available for public use.
brief.boundaryZh: 大概輪廓不是完整程序，也不表示所有細節已定；它仍有價值，但要說清目前深度，以及哪些內容仍待補充。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把輪廓當作最終承諾，也不能因別人願說概況，就要求他公開全部私人內容。
brief.outcomeZh: 能提出有用的概況，同時保留尚未知的細節，以及本人願意分享的範圍。

sources.sentence: Clothing may sketch the outline of someone's public role.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 50, table 2, row 6; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The writer sketched the outline of the story, from the lost invitation to the final meeting, but left the middle scenes open; the group could discuss its direction without pretending that every character decision had been written.
listening.zh: 作者勾勒故事的大概輪廓，從遺失邀請函到最後見面，但中間場景仍未定；小組可以討論方向，而不用假裝每個人物決定都已寫好。
listening.promptZh: 目前已有甚麼？哪些部分仍未定？

options.en: The broad beginning and ending were described, while middle scenes and decisions remained open.
options.zh: 大致的開頭與結尾已有描述，但中間場景及決定仍未定。

options.en: Every scene and line of dialogue had already been fixed in the final script.
options.zh: 每個場景及每句對白，都已在最終劇本中定下來。

options.en: The group had no information about either the starting problem or the ending.
options.zh: 小組完全不知道起始問題，也不知道結尾。

options.en: The writer had drawn detailed pictures instead of describing any story direction.
options.zh: 作者只畫了詳細圖畫，沒有說任何故事方向。

listening.explanationZh: 輪廓可以提供方向，而不必已有全部細節；不是所有內容已定，也不是一無所知，更不一定要實際畫圖。

reply.promptZh: 小組為甚麼已能討論方向，卻不能當作所有決定都已定下來？
reply.promptEn: Why could the group discuss the direction without treating every decision as settled?

options.en: The writer sketched the outline, giving a broad route but leaving the middle scenes unwritten.
options.zh: 作者勾勒了輪廓，給出大概路線，但中間場景還未寫。

options.en: We knew the starting problem and final meeting without having every link between them.
options.zh: 我們知道起始問題及最後見面，卻還沒有兩者之間的每個連結。

options.en: The account gave enough shape for discussion, not a complete script.
options.zh: 這份敘述有足夠形態供討論，但不是完整劇本。

options.en: Some character choices still needed to be developed within the proposed direction.
options.zh: 部分人物選擇仍需在所提方向中繼續發展。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋了概況與細節屬不同層次。

scene.promptZh: 另一份文件已列出每個步驟、負責人及日期，並附完整指示；同學卻只稱它為粗略輪廓。哪句較準確？

options.en: It does more than sketch the outline, because the described document supplies detailed instructions and responsibilities.
options.zh: 它不只是勾勒輪廓，因為所述文件已提供詳細指示及責任分配。

options.en: The account says the steps and responsible people are still entirely unspecified.
options.zh: 敘述說，步驟及負責人仍完全未有交代。

options.en: The dates appear only as questions for a future draft, not in the current instructions.
options.zh: 日期只列作下一稿待回答的問題，沒有出現在目前指示中。

scene.explanationZh: 應按文件目前的詳細程度描述；已給完整步驟，就不能只當作尚未細化的輪廓。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能從 sketch the outline 推論出來？

options.en: Provide the broad shape of an account.
options.zh: 提供敘述的大概形態。

options.en: Every private detail has been shared and approved for publication.
options.zh: 每項私人細節都已分享，並獲准刊出。

options.en: Leave some details for later or for the speaker’s choice.
options.zh: 某些細節可以留待稍後，或由說話者選擇是否交代。

contrast.explanationZh: 提供輪廓不等於分享全部細節，更不表示已有使用許可。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問：「有開頭和結尾，就可以說每場對白都寫完了嗎？」中間部分仍未定。哪個回應最好？

options.en: We have sketched the outline, not the full script; the middle scenes still need developing.
options.zh: 我們已勾勒輪廓，但還不是完整劇本；中間場景仍需發展。

options.en: Yes, a broad direction counts as every line already being written.
options.zh: 可以，有大概方向就算每句對白都已寫好。

options.en: There is no starting point or ending to discuss because the middle is unfinished.
options.zh: 因為中間未完成，所以沒有起點或結尾可以討論。

dialogue.explanationZh: 有概況不等於全部已好，也不能因中間留白，就抹去已有的形態。

speaking.en: I can sketch the outline of what happened, but I would like to decide which personal details I am comfortable sharing.
speaking.zh: 我可以勾勒事情的大概經過，但想自行決定哪些私人細節是我願意分享的。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清概況與分享的細節深度。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你訪問祖父搬家的回憶，他願說大致先後，卻不想談家庭衝突。你想回覆，可以先勾勒大概，不需補上他不想說的細節，再一起議定哪些話可錄下或刊出。用一至兩句英文回覆，不把願意說概況當作對所有用途都同意。
writing.selfCheckZh: 回覆要尊重受訪者選擇的深度，先談概況，再議錄音及刊出的範圍；不用一項同意取代所有私事或出版用途的許可。

examples.en: You can sketch the outline of the move without going into the family disagreements you prefer to keep private. Afterwards, we can agree which parts you would like recorded or shared, rather than assume your whole account is for publication.
examples.zh: 你可以勾勒搬家的大概經過，而不談那些想保留為私事的家庭分歧。之後我們可以議定，你願意錄下或分享哪些部分，而不是假定整段敘述都可刊出。

examples.en: Let us sketch the outline first, at the level of detail you choose. We can leave the private parts untouched and decide together what, if anything, belongs in the written account.
examples.zh: 先按你選擇的細節深度，勾勒大概輪廓吧。我們可以不碰私人部分，再一起決定是否有適合寫進敘述的內容，以及究竟是哪些。

glossary.en: the level of detail you choose

takeaways.en: She sketched the outline of the visit, leaving the exact times for a later discussion.
takeaways.zh: 她勾勒了參觀的大概安排，把確切時間留待稍後討論。

takeaways.en: The speaker could sketch the outline without being ready to explain every personal detail.
takeaways.zh: 說話者可以交代大概輪廓，同時仍未準備好解釋每項私人細節。

brief.meaningEn: Wear clothes that fit the role or impression expected in a particular situation.
brief.meaningZh: 穿着符合特定角色或場合預期形象的衣服。
brief.grammar: dress the part for a role/occasion; dressed/dressing. The phrase concerns appearance fitting the role, not proof of ability or a real qualification.
brief.register: Common role-and-theatre-related idiom. Expectations vary by stated setting; expensive clothing is not built into the meaning, and an actor’s costume does not make the actor that professional.
brief.boundaryZh: 穿得像角色，不等於真正具備資格或技能，也不一定要昂貴；應按場合明說的需要，不替所有場合作同一規定。
brief.misconceptionZh: 服裝可以服務表演或禮節，但不能取代能力證據，也不應只靠衣着判斷人的價值。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述衣着如何配合角色，分清外觀、場合要求及實際能力。

listening.en: For the school play, Ravi dressed the part of the gardener in the apron named in the director’s notes, but he still needed to practise the scene; the costume made the role visible, not the lines automatically remembered.
listening.zh: 校劇中，Ravi穿上導演筆記所寫的圍裙，穿出園丁角色的形象，但他仍需練習場景；服裝讓人看出角色，卻不表示台詞都已記住。
listening.promptZh: 服裝做到甚麼？還有甚麼需要準備？

options.en: It made the role recognisable while rehearsal of the scene remained necessary.
options.zh: 服裝讓角色容易辨認，但場景仍需要綵排。

options.en: The director had asked him only to choose clothes, with no scene practice expected.
options.zh: 導演只要求他選衣服，沒有要求練習場景。

options.en: The notes required a different character, so Ravi was ignoring the stated role.
options.zh: 筆記要求另一個角色，所以Ravi沒有按指定角色準備。

options.en: The apron established that Ravi worked professionally as a gardener outside the play.
options.zh: 圍裙確認Ravi在戲外也是職業園丁。

listening.explanationZh: 服裝按筆記呈現角色，但仍需練習；不是導演只要求選衣服，也不是角色不符或證明戲外職業。

reply.promptZh: Ravi為甚麼穿那件圍裙？
reply.promptEn: Why did Ravi wear that apron?

options.en: He wanted to dress the part of the gardener described in the play.
options.zh: 他想穿出劇中園丁角色的形象。

options.en: The director’s notes used that clothing to make the role recognisable.
options.zh: 導演筆記用這種服裝，讓觀眾容易辨認角色。

options.en: It supported the character’s appearance without doing the acting for him.
options.zh: 它支持角色的外觀，但不會替他完成演戲。

options.en: The costume matched the specific role he was preparing to perform.
options.zh: 服裝符合他正在準備演出的特定角色。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以角色外觀解釋服裝選擇，不把衣着當作真正資格的證據。

scene.promptZh: 典禮邀請只要求衣着整潔舒適，朋友卻說，要買最昂貴的西裝才算穿得合場合。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: You can dress the part by following the stated expectation; the phrase does not itself require the most expensive suit.
options.zh: 依照已說明的要求，就可以穿得合場合；這個詞組本身不要求最昂貴的西裝。

options.en: The invitation explicitly requires the highest-priced formal suit.
options.zh: 邀請明確要求穿價格最高的正式西裝。

options.en: The account says comfort is forbidden and no dress expectation has been given.
options.zh: 敘述說禁止舒適衣着，也沒有給任何服裝要求。

scene.explanationZh: 按已給的需要判斷，不用價格取代是否相襯，也不改寫邀請內容。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能從 dress the part 推論出來？

options.en: Clothing fits the expected role or occasion.
options.zh: 服裝符合預期的角色或場合。

options.en: The wearer has already proved every skill the role requires.
options.zh: 穿着者已證明自己具備角色需要的每項技能。

options.en: Relevant expectations can differ between settings.
options.zh: 相關預期可以因場合而不同。

contrast.explanationZh: 外在形象不是技能的證據。

dialogue.promptZh: 同學問Ravi：「圍裙穿好了，今天就不用練台詞吧？」台詞還未練熟。哪個回應最好？

options.en: I can dress the part, but I still need to rehearse the words and actions.
options.zh: 我可以穿得符合角色，但仍需要綵排台詞及動作。

options.en: I can spend the rehearsal adjusting the costume instead of practising the unfamiliar lines.
options.zh: 我可以把綵排時間用來調整服裝，而不練那些還不熟的台詞。

options.en: I am preparing a gardening demonstration, so I should explain the tools rather than follow the scripted dialogue.
options.zh: 我準備的是園藝示範，所以應解釋工具，不用照劇本對白。

dialogue.explanationZh: 這次是劇本演出，服裝以外仍需練台詞及動作；不把綵排改成只調衣服，也不誤當園藝示範。

speaking.en: I want to dress the part for this occasion, but I will check the actual expectations rather than assume that higher cost means a better fit.
speaking.zh: 我想穿得符合這次場合，但會先了解實際要求，不假定價格較高就比較合適。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再按角色及場合需要判斷，而不是只看價格。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友邀你參加小型頒獎慶祝，你想穿得合場合，但不想只為一次活動買新外套。你有一件整潔舊外套，想問是否符合邀請的正式程度；你不是要求朋友降低安排，也不假裝已知道規定。用一至兩句英文寫實際詢問。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出有禮而具體的服裝詢問，交代已有衣物及想了解的要求；不用價格決定合宜程度，也不先替主辦者答應。

examples.en: I would like to dress the part for the celebration without buying a jacket for one evening. Would my neat older jacket fit the level of formality you have in mind, or is there a specific expectation I should know about?
examples.zh: 我想穿得符合慶祝場合，又不想只為一晚買件外套。我那件整潔的舊外套，是否符合你心中的正式程度，還是有甚麼具體要求我應該先知道？

examples.en: I want to dress the part, and I already have a tidy jacket I would prefer to use. Could you tell me what the invitation’s dress note means for this particular gathering before I decide?
examples.zh: 我想穿得合場合，也已有一件較想使用的整潔外套。決定前，可否說明邀請上的衣着備註，在這次特定聚會是甚麼意思？

glossary.en: buying a jacket for one evening

takeaways.en: The actor dressed the part with a simple costume, then worked on the gestures that made the character believable.
takeaways.zh: 演員以簡單服裝穿出角色形象，再練習讓人物可信的動作。

takeaways.en: She asked what it meant to dress the part at that event instead of assuming every occasion required the same outfit.
takeaways.zh: 她詢問在該活動怎樣才算穿得合宜，而不假定每個場合都需要同一套衣服。

titleEn: get the wrong end of the stick

target.pattern: \b(?:get|gets|got|getting) the wrong end of the stick\b|\bgotten the wrong end of the stick\b

brief.meaningEn: Misunderstand what someone means or what a situation is about.
brief.meaningZh: 誤解別人的意思，或弄錯某件事情的情況。
brief.grammar: get/got the wrong end of the stick about something; I think you have got the wrong end of the stick. The stick image is nonliteral; identify the actual misunderstanding.
brief.register: Common informal idiom. It can acknowledge one’s own mistake or gently correct another person, but does not itself prove deliberate deception or stupidity.
brief.boundaryZh: 誤會不等於故意說謊或不聰明，也不一定是整件事都弄錯；要說明把甚麼誤解成甚麼。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要只說一句「你搞錯了」而不解釋；可以確認意思並修正具體假設，不先責怪別人的動機。
brief.outcomeZh: 能有禮地澄清具體誤會，分清原有文字、自己的理解及尚未證實的意圖。

listening.en: I got the wrong end of the stick when “bring a draft” made me think a finished article was due; the editor meant rough notes for discussion, so I asked her to confirm the level of preparation before rewriting everything.
listening.zh: 聽到「帶一份草稿」，我誤會成到時要交一篇已完成的文章；編輯其實指供討論用的粗略筆記，所以在把所有內容重寫之前，我先請她確認需要準備到甚麼程度。
listening.promptZh: 誤會在哪裏？說話者怎樣釐清？

options.en: A request for rough discussion notes was read as a finished-article deadline, then checked with the editor.
options.zh: 供討論的粗略筆記，被理解成已完成文章的限期要求，之後再向編輯確認。

options.en: The editor explicitly demanded a published article and rejected all rough notes.
options.zh: 編輯明確要求一篇已刊出的文章，並拒絕所有粗略筆記。

options.en: The writer understood the requested level from the start and needed no clarification.
options.zh: 作者一開始就明白需要準備到甚麼程度，不需要澄清。

options.en: The editor’s intent was established by a rumour rather than by asking her.
options.zh: 編輯的意思是從傳言確定的，而不是直接向她查問。

listening.explanationZh: 誤會涉及草稿的準備程度，之後有問本人；不是原先已懂、真的要刊出文章，或只靠傳言。

reply.promptZh: 作者為甚麼先問編輯，而不是直接重寫整篇文章？
reply.promptEn: Why did the writer ask before rewriting the whole article?

options.en: I had got the wrong end of the stick about what counted as a draft and wanted to confirm it.
options.zh: 我誤會了「草稿」所指的程度，所以想先確認。

options.en: I had assumed a finished article was required, but the editor meant rough notes.
options.zh: 我原以為要交完成的文章，但編輯指的是粗略筆記。

options.en: Clarifying the preparation level could prevent work based on the wrong expectation.
options.zh: 問清楚需要準備到甚麼程度，可以避免按錯誤預期做事。

options.en: The uncertainty concerned what to bring, not a confirmed decision to reject the article.
options.zh: 不確定的是要帶甚麼，並不是編輯已決定拒絕文章。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都回應了具體誤會及先確認的理由，沒有添加故意刁難的動機。

scene.promptZh: 同學看到通知「周五前先別改」，就問是否等收到回饋再改，並得到確認；她沒有把它當成永久不准修改。哪句準確？

options.en: She checked the meaning instead of getting the wrong end of the stick and treating a temporary pause as a permanent ban.
options.zh: 她先確認意思，沒有誤把暫時停改當成永久禁止。

options.en: She concluded that the work could never be revised and did not ask anyone.
options.zh: 她沒有問任何人，就斷定作品永遠不能再修改。

options.en: The reply confirmed a permanent ban rather than waiting for feedback.
options.zh: 回覆確認的是永久禁止，而不是等回饋。

scene.explanationZh: 她已查問並確認只是暫停，不能再替她加上誤會或永久禁令。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只從 get the wrong end of the stick 推論出來？

options.en: Someone has misunderstood a point.
options.zh: 有人誤解了某一點。

options.en: The other person deliberately lied to cause the mistake.
options.zh: 另一人故意說謊，讓這次誤會發生。

options.en: A clear explanation can identify what was misread.
options.zh: 清楚的解釋可以指出甚麼被誤讀。

contrast.explanationZh: 理解錯誤本身，不會同時提供別人有惡意的證據。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「你沒有帶完成稿，是故意不配合嗎？」編輯原本只要求粗略筆記。哪個回應最好？

options.en: I think you have got the wrong end of the stick: she asked for rough notes to discuss, not a finished article.
options.zh: 我想你誤會了：她要的是用來討論的粗略筆記，不是完成的文章。

options.en: Yes, rough notes and a finished article are the same level of preparation.
options.zh: 是的，粗略筆記和完成文章，屬於同樣的準備程度。

options.en: The editor has already rejected the article, although we have not discussed it yet.
options.zh: 雖然我們還未討論，編輯卻已經拒絕那篇文章。

dialogue.explanationZh: 直接解釋要求的差異，不用惡意標籤，也不添加尚未發生的決定。

speaking.en: I may have got the wrong end of the stick, so could you explain whether you want rough notes or a complete draft?
speaking.zh: 我可能誤會了，所以可否說明，你想要的是粗略筆記，還是一份完整草稿？
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再用具體選項釐清意思。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友說暫時不想公開她的詩，你誤以為她拒絕跟你交流，便冷淡回覆；現在才知道，她仍想私下聽回饋。你想道歉，說清自己誤讀了甚麼，再問她現在想怎樣分享，而不要求她因此同意公開。用一至兩句英文寫訊息。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出承認自己誤讀的道歉及詢問，清楚區分私下交流與公開；不把修補關係變成要求對方給予新許可。

examples.en: I got the wrong end of the stick and read your wish for privacy as a rejection of our conversation. I am sorry for the cold reply; would you like to share the poem privately, and what kind of feedback would feel useful now?
examples.zh: 我誤會了，把你想保留私隱，讀成拒絕我們的交流。對不起，我回覆得很冷淡；你想私下分享那首詩嗎？現在甚麼回饋會對你有用？

examples.en: I think I got the wrong end of the stick about what you meant by not sharing publicly. I would like to listen on the terms you choose, without expecting you to agree to publication because I misunderstood.
examples.zh: 我想我誤會了你說「不公開分享」的意思。我願意按你選擇的條件聆聽，不會因自己誤會過，就期望你同意刊出。

takeaways.en: He got the wrong end of the stick about the invitation and asked which part of the meeting was open to visitors.
takeaways.zh: 他誤解了邀請，於是詢問聚會哪個部分開放給訪客。

takeaways.en: She thought she had got the wrong end of the stick, so she checked the message before assigning blame.
takeaways.zh: 她想自己可能誤會了，所以在追究責任之前，先確認訊息。

titleEn: judge a book by its cover

brief.meaningEn: Form a judgement about a person or thing from outward appearance rather than relevant underlying qualities.
brief.meaningZh: 只根據人或物的外表作判斷，而沒有考慮相關的內在特質。
brief.grammar: do not judge a book by its cover; judging/judged. The proverb applies beyond actual books; it warns against treating appearance as sufficient evidence, not against noticing any relevant presentation requirement.
brief.register: Familiar proverb/idiom. Examine what actually matters for the task; outward details may prompt questions but do not settle ability, character or quality on their own.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是說任何外觀都毫無資訊，而是不能單憑外表下結論；場合明訂的要求仍可另作確認。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要因衣服樸素便判能力差，也不因外觀漂亮就當內容很好；需要相關的實際證據。
brief.outcomeZh: 能提出公平的評價根據，分清表面印象與可以檢視的能力或品質。

listening.en: Some volunteers doubted the newcomer because his shirt had paint stains, though his checklist helped organise the display; the coordinator said not to judge a book by its cover and asked them to examine his contribution.
listening.zh: 一些義工因新成員的襯衫有油漆漬而懷疑他，但他的清單卻幫忙整理了展示；統籌提醒大家不要只憑表面判斷，並請他們看實際貢獻。
listening.promptZh: 原先判斷依據是甚麼？哪些證據更相關？

options.en: A stained shirt prompted doubt, while the useful checklist showed an actual contribution.
options.zh: 襯衫污漬引起懷疑，但有用的清單顯示了實際貢獻。

options.en: The checklist was never used because the shirt proved the member could not organise anything.
options.zh: 襯衫證明他不會統籌任何事情，所以清單從來沒有被使用。

options.en: The coordinator decided he could help only with painting, rather than planning.
options.zh: 統籌決定他只可以幫忙油漆，而不能參與規劃。

options.en: The group examined the checklist first and questioned its contents, rather than reacting to his shirt.
options.zh: 小組先查看清單並質疑內容，而不是對衣服作反應。

listening.explanationZh: 衣漬不能決定能力，實際清單卻有幫助；不是統籌限制他只能油漆，也不是先看內容才提出質疑。

reply.promptZh: 統籌為甚麼請大家查看實際貢獻？
reply.promptEn: Why did the coordinator ask the group to examine the actual contribution?

options.en: They were judging a book by its cover when they doubted him from the paint-stained shirt.
options.zh: 大家因有油漆漬的襯衫而懷疑他，是在只憑表面判斷。

options.en: His checklist gave more relevant evidence of how he helped the display.
options.zh: 清單提供了更相關的證據，顯示他如何幫助展示工作。

options.en: The outward stain did not establish that he lacked organisational care.
options.zh: 外在污漬不能確定他缺乏統籌時所需的細心。

options.en: The useful work challenged an assumption made before examining his contribution.
options.zh: 有用的工作，挑戰了大家未看貢獻前就作出的假設。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都回應外表與相關工作證據的差別，不是說外觀在任何情況都沒有作用。

scene.promptZh: 一個桌遊盒很樸素，但試玩後，大家認為規則清楚、互動有趣；朋友仍只按盒面說內容差。哪句最好？

options.en: Calling the game poor from the plain box would judge a book by its cover rather than use the play experience.
options.zh: 只因盒子樸素就說遊戲差，是只憑表面判斷，而沒有使用實際試玩的經驗。

options.en: The plain box suggests poorly explained rules, so the group should discount their successful trial.
options.zh: 樸素的盒子讓人覺得規則解釋差，所以小組不應重視自己順利試玩的經驗。

options.en: The account says the group has not yet tried the game or discussed the rules.
options.zh: 敘述說，小組還未試玩，也未討論規則。

scene.explanationZh: 已有實際試玩的資料，不應只憑盒面否定它，也不能說小組尚未試過。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合「不要只憑表面判斷」的提醒？

options.en: Look for qualities relevant to the actual task.
options.zh: 尋找跟實際任務相關的特質。

options.en: Assume attractive presentation proves the content is already excellent.
options.zh: 假定呈現漂亮，就證明內容已經優秀。

options.en: Distinguish a first impression from a supported judgement.
options.zh: 分清第一印象與有根據的判斷。

contrast.explanationZh: 漂亮外觀也不能代替內容優秀的證據。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴問：「他的衣服有漬，就不用看那張清單吧？」清單已幫大家整理展示。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Let us not judge a book by its cover; the checklist is relevant evidence of what he has contributed.
options.zh: 別只憑表面判斷；清單是他作出貢獻的相關證據。

options.en: Yes, a shirt stain settles whether his planning can be useful.
options.zh: 是的，襯衫污漬已足以決定他的規劃是否有用。

options.en: The useful checklist is enough to decide his suitability for the reception task, without checking that task’s practical requirements.
options.zh: 只靠有用的清單，就足以決定他是否適合接待工作，不需再看該工作有甚麼實際要求。

dialogue.explanationZh: 應按相關證據公平評價；清單能顯示貢獻，但也不能單憑它決定另一職務的所有要求。

speaking.en: I do not want to judge a book by its cover, so I will look at the work and the needs of this task before deciding.
speaking.zh: 我不想只憑表面判斷，所以作決定前，會先看作品及這次任務的實際需要。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出跟任務相關的證據。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你邀朋友到一間外觀樸素的社區小廳看新劇，她只見照片便說不值得去。你有劇目簡介，但不知道她喜歡哪類演出；你想請她先看內容再選，不保證她一定喜歡，也不說華麗場地都不好。用一至兩句英文寫有禮的邀請。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫不強迫的邀請，提供內容作選擇資料，而不保證喜歡；也不把反對外貌偏見，倒轉成樸素必好或華麗必差。

examples.en: Please do not judge a book by its cover from the plain hall alone; the programme will tell you more about the play. Would you like to read it and decide whether the story interests you, rather than feel obliged to come just because I invited you?
examples.zh: 請別只憑小廳樸素的外觀，就對演出下結論；節目簡介能讓你更了解這齣戲。你想先讀讀，再決定故事是否吸引你嗎？不用只因我邀請，就覺得一定要來。

examples.en: I would rather not judge a book by its cover when choosing this performance. I can send you the synopsis so you can decide for yourself, without promising that a simple venue makes the play right for everyone.
examples.zh: 選這場演出時，我不想只憑表面判斷。我可以把劇情簡介傳給你，讓你自行決定，而不保證簡單的場地就讓這齣戲適合所有人。

takeaways.en: She refused to judge a book by its cover and read the proposal before deciding whether it met the group’s needs.
takeaways.zh: 她不願只憑表面判斷，先讀提案，再決定是否符合小組需要。

takeaways.en: Not judging a book by its cover means asking for relevant evidence, not assuming that every first impression must be wrong.
takeaways.zh: 不憑表面判斷，是要求相關證據，而不是假定每個第一印象一定錯。

target.pattern: \b(?:clothes may speak|a uniform speaks before the person does)\b

brief.meaningEn: Clothing can communicate an impression or association without words, through a personification of clothes.
brief.meaningZh: 把衣物擬人化，表示衣着不用言語，也可能傳達某種印象或聯想。
brief.grammar: clothes may speak before someone talks; may preserves possibility. A uniform speaks before the person does is the singular uniform version of the same personification; does stands for speaks. Both describe an impression arising before conversation, not proof of the wearer’s actual role or authority. Explain the observer’s reading and check it against the wearer’s account.
brief.register: Creative personification, not a fixed rule or literal speaking garment. A signal can be unintended or interpreted differently; appearance alone does not reveal a complete personality or intention.
brief.boundaryZh: 衣物不是真的開口說話，印象也不保證就是穿着者的原意或完整身份；要分清本人解釋、觀察者聯想與共同背景。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不同人可以讀出不同意思；應向本人查問，而不是只憑衣服決定他的性格或職權。
brief.outcomeZh: 能解釋衣着提供的非語言提示及解讀差異，再用本人的說法補充，不只依靠外表。
