listening.en: Their grandfather’s patched coat brought memories to the cousins, while a visitor saw only an old garment. “Clothes may speak,” my aunt said, “but what you hear can depend on what you already know.”
listening.zh: 祖父補過的外套，讓幾位表親想起往事，但訪客只看見一件舊衣。姨母說：「衣物也許會說話，但你聽到甚麼，可能取決於你原先知道甚麼。」
listening.promptZh: 同一件衣物為甚麼會有不同意義？

options.en: The cousins knew a family connection that the visitor did not share.
options.zh: 幾位表親知道一段家庭連結，但訪客沒有這段共同背景。

options.en: Every observer had already heard the same complete history of the coat.
options.zh: 每位觀察者都已聽過同一段完整的外套歷史。

options.en: The visitor had made the coat and explained its meaning to the cousins.
options.zh: 訪客製作了那件外套，再向表親解釋它的意思。

options.en: The cousins saw a new garment with no link to anyone they knew.
options.zh: 幾位表親看見一件新衣，跟自己認識的人沒有關聯。

listening.explanationZh: 共有背景會令聯想不同；沒有說所有人都已聽過同一歷史，也沒有說外套由訪客製作。

reply.promptZh: 姨母為甚麼把衣着的意義，連到觀察者原先知道的事？
reply.promptEn: Why did the aunt connect the clothing’s meaning with what the observer already knew?

options.en: Clothes may speak through associations, but the cousins’ memories were not shared by the visitor.
options.zh: 衣物可以透過聯想傳意，但訪客並不擁有幾位表親的回憶。

options.en: The same visible coat connected to a person the cousins remembered.
options.zh: 同一件可見的外套，連到幾位表親記得的那個人。

options.en: Seeing an old garment did not give the visitor the family story behind it.
options.zh: 看見舊衣，並不會讓訪客同時知道背後的家庭故事。

options.en: The different responses showed that appearance did not carry one complete explanation for everyone.
options.zh: 不同反應顯示，外觀沒有向每個人提供同一個完整解釋。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以共有背景及不同反應解釋，不把衣着當成能自行交代全部故事。

scene.promptZh: 同學看見朋友穿某個圖案，就說她一定想傳達某種訊息，但朋友尚未解釋選衣原因。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: Clothes may speak to the observer, but we should ask what the wearer intended before treating that reading as fact.
options.zh: 衣物可能對觀察者傳達印象，但把解讀當成事實前，應先問穿着者的原意。

options.en: The observer’s first association confirms the wearer’s exact intention.
options.zh: 觀察者的第一個聯想，已確認穿着者的確切意圖。

options.en: The wearer has already given a full explanation, so no interpretation is being assumed.
options.zh: 穿着者已作完整解釋，所以目前沒有任何未確認的解讀。

scene.explanationZh: 保留可能的訊號，以及本人尚未解釋的狀態，不把自己的聯想當作確認。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能從 clothes may speak 的意象推論出來？

options.en: Clothing can suggest an impression before words are exchanged.
options.zh: 雙方尚未交談，衣着已可能提示某種印象。

options.en: The observer necessarily knows the wearer’s complete personality and intention.
options.zh: 觀察者必定知道穿着者完整的性格及意圖。

options.en: Different backgrounds can lead to different readings.
options.zh: 不同背景可以帶來不同解讀。

contrast.explanationZh: 可能的提示，不等於完全知道一個人的內心。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友問：「我看見那圖案就想到節慶，她穿它一定也是想表達這意思吧？」穿着者還未解釋。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Clothes may speak, but your association is not yet her explanation; why not ask what she likes about it?
options.zh: 衣物也許會傳意，但你的聯想還不是她的解釋；何不問問她喜歡它哪一點？

options.en: Yes, your first reading settles her reason for choosing it.
options.zh: 是的，你的第一個解讀已確定她選衣的原因。

options.en: She has already told us that it has the meaning you guessed, although we have not asked her.
options.zh: 雖然我們還未問，她卻已告訴我們，那正是你猜的意思。

dialogue.explanationZh: 直接提出自然的詢問，不把自己的解讀代替本人的話，也不添加尚未得到的確認。

speaking.en: Clothes may speak, but I would rather hear the wearer’s own explanation than turn my first impression into a fact about them.
speaking.zh: 衣物也許會傳意，但我寧願聽穿着者自己的解釋，而不是把第一印象變成關於他的事實。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清訊號、解讀及本人的解釋。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你穿得正式，是為了祝賀得獎朋友，旁人卻把你當作主持人。你想有禮澄清自己只是賓客，並表達祝賀；不說誤認的人笨，也不否認衣着確實可能給人印象。用一至兩句英文寫出實際開場話。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出可直接說的開場澄清，承認衣着可能帶來印象，同時說清本人的角色及祝賀目的；不貶低誤認者，也不冒認主持權限。

examples.en: Clothes may speak, and my suit seems to have suggested that I am hosting, but I am here as a guest. I dressed for the occasion to celebrate my friend, and I am very happy to join you in congratulating her.
examples.zh: 衣着也許會傳意，我這套西裝似乎讓人以為我是主持，但我其實是賓客。我是為慶祝朋友而穿得合場合，很高興跟大家一起祝賀她。

examples.en: If clothes may speak, mine have apparently given me a role I do not have tonight. I am simply a guest who wanted to honour a friend’s achievement, so let me add my congratulations rather than take over the programme.
examples.zh: 若衣着真能傳意，我這身裝扮顯然替我安排了今晚不屬於我的角色。我只是想向朋友的成就致敬的賓客，所以讓我加上一句祝賀，而不是接管整個流程。

takeaways.en: Clothes may speak through shared associations, but the meaning is not always the one a stranger first imagines.
takeaways.zh: 衣物可以透過共有的聯想傳意，但意思不一定就是陌生人第一個想像的那樣。

takeaways.en: She said clothes may speak, then asked the wearer what the borrowed jacket meant to him.
takeaways.zh: 她說衣物也許會傳意，接着問穿着者，那件借來的外套對他有何意義。

brief.meaningEn: Quiet and deliberately unobtrusive in manner or presentation, rather than highly public or elaborate.
brief.meaningZh: 在態度或呈現方式上安靜、不張揚，不刻意大肆公開或鋪張。
brief.grammar: remain/be low-key; a low-key response or event. The adjective describes manner or scale, not necessarily the person’s happiness, success or the quality of the work.
brief.register: Common descriptive compound. Respect the person’s stated preference; quiet gratitude can be genuine, and a low-key person can create bold work.
brief.boundaryZh: 低調不等於不開心、能力低或作品沒有特色；不張揚也不必完全隱瞞。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要只因安靜就判斷為冷漠，也不把公開慶祝當作唯一表達關心的方法。
brief.outcomeZh: 能按本人偏好描述低調方式，分清呈現方法、成就及感受。

listening.en: After her illustration won a prize, Nia kept the response low-key: she thanked the group in a short private note and said she was delighted, but preferred not to make a public announcement that week.
listening.zh: 插畫得獎後，Nia保持低調：她私下寫短箋感謝小組，並說自己很高興，但那一周較想不作公開宣布。
listening.promptZh: 她的低調表現在哪裏？不能改寫成甚麼？

options.en: She expressed happiness and gratitude privately while declining a public announcement for that week.
options.zh: 她私下表達高興及感謝，同時不想在那一周公開宣布。

options.en: She was disappointed with the prize and refused to thank the group.
options.zh: 她對獎項感到失望，也拒絕感謝小組。

options.en: She asked the group to arrange a large public announcement immediately.
options.zh: 她要求小組立即安排大型公開宣布。

options.en: Her note announced that she was leaving illustration rather than continuing her work.
options.zh: 她的短箋宣布不再繼續插畫工作，而是要離開這個領域。

listening.explanationZh: 低調體現在私下短箋及不公開；她明說高興並表達感謝，沒有說要退出插畫。

reply.promptZh: Nia為甚麼用私下短箋回應？
reply.promptEn: Why did Nia respond in a private note?

options.en: She wanted a low-key response while still thanking the people who helped.
options.zh: 她想低調回應，同時感謝幫助過她的人。

options.en: She preferred to share her delight privately rather than announce the prize publicly that week.
options.zh: 那一周，她較想私下分享喜悅，而不公開宣布得獎。

options.en: A short note suited the quiet manner she wanted for acknowledging the support.
options.zh: 短箋配合她想安靜答謝支援的方式。

options.en: She could express real gratitude without making the news a public event.
options.zh: 她可以表達真誠感謝，而不把消息變成公開活動。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以她偏好的呈現方式作解釋，不推斷她失望或不重視別人。

scene.promptZh: 一位畫家在訪問中說話低調，畫作卻用大面積鮮色及強烈線條；旁人以為 low-key 必定指畫面柔淡。哪句準確？

options.en: Her manner can be low-key even though the paintings themselves are bold.
options.zh: 她的態度可以低調，畫作本身卻仍然大膽鮮明。

options.en: The description says her paintings use only faint colours and delicate lines.
options.zh: 描述說，她的畫作只用淡色及纖細線條。

options.en: The strong colours show that she prefers an elaborate public response in every interview.
options.zh: 強烈色彩顯示，她在每次訪問都較想大肆公開回應。

scene.explanationZh: 人的態度與作品風格是兩個方面，不能把一方的特點硬套到另一方。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只從 low-key 這個描述推論出來？

options.en: The presentation avoids attracting a great deal of public attention.
options.zh: 呈現方式避免引起大量公眾注意。

options.en: The person is necessarily unhappy with the achievement.
options.zh: 當事人必定對這項成就感到不開心。

options.en: A sincere response can be quiet rather than elaborate.
options.zh: 真誠的回應可以安靜，而不必鋪張。

contrast.explanationZh: 低調描述方式，不足以判斷當事人是否為成就感到高興。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友問：「她只私下感謝我們，是不是不高興得獎？」Nia已說很開心，只是不想那一周公開。哪個回應最好？

options.en: She said she was delighted; a low-key thank-you is simply how she wants to share it this week.
options.zh: 她說自己很高興；低調答謝只是她這一周想分享的方式。

options.en: I think she is disappointed with the result, despite what she said about being delighted.
options.zh: 雖然她說很高興，我卻認為她對結果失望。

options.en: Let us publish the announcement now; her private thanks should count as agreement to that.
options.zh: 現在就公開宣布吧；她私下感謝，就應當作已同意公開。

dialogue.explanationZh: 按本人明說的感受及公開偏好回應，不憑方式否定感受，也不擅自代她同意。

speaking.en: A low-key response can be sincere; I would ask how she wants to share the news rather than assume that quiet means unhappy.
speaking.zh: 低調回應也可以真誠；我會先問她想怎樣分享消息，而不假定安靜就是不開心。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清回應方式與本人的感受。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友沒有獲選展覽，暫時不想在群組談結果。你想私下低調支持，讓她選擇是否一起喝茶，也可暫不回覆，而不擅自安排集體打氣。用一至兩句英文寫真實訊息。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出有選擇權的私下支持，尊重暫不公開及暫不回覆；不把低調當冷淡，也不替朋友決定集體活動。

examples.en: I would like to keep my support low-key and respect your wish not to discuss the result in the group. If you would welcome some company over tea, I am here, but there is no need to reply now.
examples.zh: 我想保持低調地支持你，尊重你不想在群組談結果的意願。如果你想有人陪着喝茶，我在這裏，但現在不需要回覆。

examples.en: We can keep this low-key: I will not start a group discussion or arrange a surprise gathering. Let me know if a quiet cup of tea would help, whenever you feel ready to answer.
examples.zh: 我們可以低調處理：我不會開群組討論，也不會安排驚喜聚會。等你準備好回答時，再告訴我，安靜喝杯茶會不會有幫助。

glossary.en: discuss the result in the group
there is no need to reply now

takeaways.en: Her low-key reply thanked the helpers without turning the prize into a public celebration.
takeaways.zh: 她用低調的回覆感謝幫助者，沒有把得獎變成公開慶祝。

takeaways.en: They chose a low-key welcome with a short conversation, because their guest had asked for a quiet evening.
takeaways.zh: 客人說想安靜過一晚，所以他們以一段短談作為低調的歡迎。

titleZh: 複雜事情中的一個因素

brief.meaningEn: One contributing factor or part of an explanation that needs other information for a fuller understanding.
brief.meaningZh: 構成影響的一個因素，或解釋的一部分；要較完整理解事情，仍需其他資訊。
brief.grammar: Attendance is only one piece of the puzzle; one/a piece of the puzzle. A piece here is a contributing part, not necessarily information previously missing or a sufficient explanation on its own.
brief.register: Conventional puzzle metaphor. Name the factor and what else matters rather than using the image to avoid a concrete explanation.
brief.boundaryZh: 一部分不是全盤，也不一定是最後補上的缺失資料；單一數字不能說明所有人的體驗。
brief.misconceptionZh: 有一個因素，不等於已知道全部；資訊不完整，也不表示它毫無參考價值。
brief.outcomeZh: 能解釋某項證據的有限作用，並指出仍需要了解的另一面。

listening.en: Attendance was one piece of the puzzle when we reviewed the open day: many visitors came, but we also needed to ask whether they could follow the activities and find someone to answer their questions.
listening.zh: 檢視開放日時，出席人數只是其中一個因素：雖然來了很多訪客，但我們仍需要了解，他們能否跟得上活動，以及是否找得到人解答問題。
listening.promptZh: 人數提供了甚麼資訊？還需要了解甚麼？

options.en: It showed turnout, while understanding and access to help still needed checking.
options.zh: 人數顯示了到場情況，但理解程度及求助渠道仍需了解。

options.en: The number alone established that every visitor understood the activities.
options.zh: 單憑人數，就已確立每位訪客都明白活動。

options.en: The review excluded attendance and considered only the colour of the posters.
options.zh: 檢視完全不看出席人數，只考慮海報顏色。

options.en: Visitor interviews had already answered every question before the review began.
options.zh: 檢視開始前，訪客訪問已解答所有問題。

listening.explanationZh: 人數有參考價值，但只反映一面，不能取代理解及求助的經驗；也未說訪問已經完成。

reply.promptZh: 檢視開放日為甚麼不能只看出席人數？
reply.promptEn: Why did the review need more than the attendance figure?

options.en: Attendance was one piece of the puzzle, not a full account of whether visitors could take part and get help.
options.zh: 人數只是其中一部分，未完整說明訪客能否參與並得到幫助。

options.en: Many people arriving did not tell us how clearly they understood the activities.
options.zh: 很多人到場，並沒有告訴我們，他們對活動理解得多清楚。

options.en: We still needed visitors’ experiences of following the sessions and finding answers.
options.zh: 我們仍需了解訪客跟隨活動，以及找到解答的體驗。

options.en: Turnout mattered, but the review also concerned what people could actually do once they arrived.
options.zh: 到場人數重要，但檢視也關乎人們到場後實際能做甚麼。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明評估還包括參與及支援，不把人數當作已足夠或完全無用。

scene.promptZh: 一張家族照片標示祖母某年曾在海邊，卻未說她何時搬家；日記及信件仍未查閱。哪句準確？

options.en: The photograph is one piece of the puzzle, but it does not by itself establish the date of her move.
options.zh: 照片是理解事情的一部分，但本身未能確定她搬家的日期。

options.en: The photograph records the exact moving date, so the remaining documents are irrelevant.
options.zh: 照片記錄了確切搬家日期，所以餘下文件都不相關。

options.en: Because the photograph is incomplete evidence, it tells us nothing about where she was that year.
options.zh: 照片證據不完整，所以完全不能說明她那年曾在哪裏。

scene.explanationZh: 照片能顯示那年曾在海邊，但不能取代搬家日期的資料；有限不等於無用。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 one piece of the puzzle 的意思？

options.en: A factor contributes to a fuller account.
options.zh: 一個因素有助形成較完整的說明。

options.en: That factor alone necessarily settles the whole explanation.
options.zh: 那個因素本身必定足以完整解釋整件事。

options.en: Other evidence may change how the factor is understood.
options.zh: 其他證據可能改變我們理解該因素的方式。

contrast.explanationZh: 部分因素，不一定足以獨自解釋全局。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「既然來了這麼多人，可以直接說人人都得到需要的幫助嗎？」目前還未問訪客。哪個回應最好？

options.en: The turnout is one piece of the puzzle; let us ask how easily visitors found help before making that claim.
options.zh: 到場人數只是其中一部分；作出這項判斷前，先問訪客找到幫助是否方便。

options.en: Yes, a large turnout is enough evidence that the help arrangements worked for everyone.
options.zh: 可以，大量人到場，已足以證明求助安排對每個人都有效。

options.en: We should leave turnout out of the review altogether, since it cannot answer every question.
options.zh: 既然人數不能回答所有問題，就應完全不把它放進檢視。

dialogue.explanationZh: 既使用人數資料，也保留其限制，再補充真正需要的訪客經驗；不以部分代全部，也不完全放棄這項資料。

speaking.en: That figure is one piece of the puzzle; I would connect it with people’s experiences before claiming to understand the whole situation.
speaking.zh: 那個數字只是其中一部分；聲稱已理解整件事之前，我會連同人們的體驗一起看。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明這個因素有何用，以及仍缺哪一面。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友昨晚沒有接你的電話，你一度以為她不在乎你，但你不知道她當時在做甚麼。你想承認自己只看見一部分，問她何時方便談，而不先判斷她的動機。用一至兩句英文寫真誠訊息。
writing.selfCheckZh: 把未接電話當作有限資料，承認自己不知道背景，再提出可回應的邀請；不直接把沉默判成拒絕或不在乎。

examples.en: The missed call is only one piece of the puzzle, and I do not know what was happening for you last night. Could you tell me when it would be a good time to talk, rather than let me guess what your silence meant?
examples.zh: 沒接的電話只是其中一部分，我不知道你昨晚有甚麼事情。可否告訴我，何時方便談，而不是讓我猜測你的沉默代表甚麼？

examples.en: I treated one unanswered call as if it explained how you felt about me, but it is only a piece of the puzzle. I would rather ask about your evening and find a time that suits us both.
examples.zh: 我把一次沒接電話，當作已能解釋你怎樣看我，但那只是其中一部分。我寧願問問你那晚的情況，再找一個適合我們雙方的時間。

glossary.en: what was happening for you last night
a time that suits us both

takeaways.en: The repair date was one piece of the puzzle; the old letters helped explain why the family had left before it.
takeaways.zh: 維修日期只是其中一部分；舊信幫忙解釋了家人為甚麼在那之前已經離開。

takeaways.en: Her account supplied one piece of the puzzle, and the interviewer asked what the other witnesses had seen.
takeaways.zh: 她的敘述提供其中一部分，訪問者再追問其他目擊者看見甚麼。

brief.meaningEn: When the circumstances require or make a particular action or choice appropriate.
brief.meaningZh: 當實際情況需要某項行動，或使某種選擇合適時。
brief.grammar: when the moment calls for an example; when the occasion calls for it/them. Call for here means require or make appropriate, not call someone by telephone; the following noun or pronoun names what is needed.
brief.register: Natural conditional usage built on call for. Explain the relevant circumstances rather than treating one option as always appropriate.
brief.boundaryZh: 是否合適要看情況，不是所有時候都需多說、穿得正式或增加安排；代詞也應有清楚的所指。
brief.misconceptionZh: 某次場合有需要，不表示該行動已完成，也不表示可以不看對方問題就套用同一做法。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把選擇連到具體需要，用條件句保留不同場合的差異。

listening.en: I add an example when the moment calls for one, such as when a listener asks how an idea works in practice; if the question only concerns the meeting time, I answer that directly rather than give another long explanation.
listening.zh: 場合需要時，我才會加一個例子，例如聽者問想法如何實際運作；如果問題只是聚會時間，我就直接回答，而不再作長篇解釋。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼時候需要例子？甚麼時候直接回答就可以？

options.en: A practical question may need an example, while a question about the time gets a direct answer.
options.zh: 問實際運作時，可能需要例子；問時間則直接回答。

options.en: Every question receives the same extended example regardless of its purpose.
options.zh: 不管問題目的，每次都給同一個長篇例子。

options.en: The speaker avoids practical examples even when asked how the idea works.
options.zh: 即使被問想法如何運作，說話者仍避免提供實際例子。

options.en: The listener had already asked to cancel the meeting rather than check its time.
options.zh: 聽者已要求取消聚會，而不是確認時間。

listening.explanationZh: 按對方實際問題作選擇，不是每次都長篇解釋、從不舉例，或把確認時間改成取消聚會。

reply.promptZh: 說話者為甚麼不在每個回答都加上長篇例子？
reply.promptEn: Why does the speaker not add a long example to every answer?

options.en: I use one when the moment calls for it, not when a direct answer to the time is enough.
options.zh: 場合需要時，我才用例子；直接答時間已足夠時就不用。

options.en: The response should fit what the listener is actually asking.
options.zh: 回應應該配合聽者實際想問的內容。

options.en: A question about the meeting time does not need the same practical explanation as a question about the idea.
options.zh: 問聚會時間，不需要跟問想法如何實踐一樣的解釋。

options.en: Adding detail without considering the question could obscure the simple answer the listener needs.
options.zh: 不考慮問題就加細節，可能掩蓋聽者需要的簡單答案。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都按問題需要解釋做法，不是說例子在任何情況都沒有用。

scene.promptZh: 訪問者剛問完問題，受訪者說「讓我想一下」；你想留短暫安靜讓她思考，而不是立即再問三題。哪句合適？

options.en: I can allow a pause when the moment calls for it, as it does while she considers this question.
options.zh: 場合需要時，我可以留一個停頓，例如她正在思考這個問題。

options.en: Her request to think means the interview has definitely ended.
options.zh: 她要求時間思考，表示訪問肯定已經結束。

options.en: Her request indicates that she wants the interviewer to answer the question on her behalf.
options.zh: 她的要求表示，她想讓訪問者代她回答問題。

scene.explanationZh: 此刻需要讓對方思考，不能推斷訪問已結束，也未說她要由訪問者代答。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能從 when the moment calls for 推論出來？

options.en: A particular circumstance makes a response appropriate.
options.zh: 某項具體情況使一個回應變得合適。

options.en: The same response must be used in every circumstance.
options.zh: 所有情況都必須使用同一個回應。

options.en: The needed thing should be clear from the following words or context.
options.zh: 後文或情境應清楚交代需要的是甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 這個條件短語保留場合差異，不是訂立一律相同的做法。

dialogue.promptZh: 聽者問：「會議幾點開始？」你知道是三點；朋友建議再講整個項目的例子。哪個回應最好？

options.en: I give examples when the moment calls for them; here I can simply say that the meeting starts at three.
options.zh: 場合需要時才舉例；這裏我只需說會議三點開始。

options.en: I will explain the whole project first, even though the only question is about the starting time.
options.zh: 即使唯一問題是開始時間，我也會先解釋整個項目。

options.en: I should avoid saying the time because a short answer would not address the question.
options.zh: 我應避免說時間，因為簡短回答不算回應問題。

dialogue.explanationZh: 直接回答所問，同時保留其他場合可能需要例子；不以篇幅長短決定是否有回答問題。

speaking.en: I can offer more detail when the moment calls for it, but I first need to understand what the other person is asking.
speaking.zh: 場合需要時，我可以提供更多細節，但首先要明白對方實際在問甚麼。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把做法連到具體的實際需要。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友希望你答應每天陪她排練，你卻只能在她遇到特定難處時另約時段，不能承諾每天到場。用一至兩句英文有禮說明自己能提供的有條件支持，請她先指出最需要幫忙的部分，不假裝已答應每天陪練。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出能守住的有條件支持，保留不能每天到場的界線，並請對方說明具體難處；不把建議當作已答應所有要求。

examples.en: I can arrange a separate session when the moment calls for focused help, but I cannot promise to come every day. Tell me which part is giving you trouble so that we can agree on a useful time together.
examples.zh: 需要集中幫忙時，我可以另約一節，但不能承諾每天到場。請告訴我哪個部分令你有困難，讓我們一起議定有用的時間。

examples.en: I would like to help when the occasion calls for it, rather than agree to a daily commitment I cannot keep. Could we identify the difficult passage first and then arrange one session around that need?
examples.zh: 有實際需要時，我想提供幫忙，而不是答應自己無法做到的每日承諾。可否先找出那個困難段落，再按這項需要安排一節？

glossary.en: which part is giving you trouble
a daily commitment I cannot keep
glossary.zh: 我無法做到的每日承諾

takeaways.en: She used a brief example when the moment called for one, then returned to the question about the plan.
takeaways.zh: 場合需要時，她用一個短例子，再回到有關計劃的問題。

takeaways.en: We can change the arrangement when the occasion calls for it, after asking which need the change would address.
takeaways.zh: 我們可以在場合需要時改安排，但先問這個改動要回應哪項需要。

brief.meaningEn: Reveal or suggest a history, experience or meaning through the details of an object or collection.
brief.meaningZh: 透過物件或一組資料的細節，呈現或暗示背後的歷史、經歷或意義。

brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體痕跡描述有根據的背景，分清已看見的細節與仍待了解的事。

listening.en: The worn handles and repeated repairs tell a story about how often the community used the old cupboard, but they do not identify who made each repair; the curator plans to ask former volunteers before naming anyone.
listening.zh: 磨損的把手及反覆修補的痕跡，呈現社區經常使用舊櫃子的經歷，但沒有指明每次由誰修補；策展人打算先問昔日義工，再寫出人名。
listening.promptZh: 物件細節支持甚麼？還需要查問哪些資訊？

options.en: The cupboard shows repeated use and repair, while the repairers’ identities remain to be checked.
options.zh: 櫃子顯示反覆使用及修補，但維修者身份仍待核實。

options.en: Each mark is already linked to a named volunteer in the account.
options.zh: 敘述已把每道痕跡，連到一位具名義工。

options.en: The visible marks come from a single recent repair rather than repeated community use.
options.zh: 可見痕跡來自最近的一次修補，而不是社區反覆使用。

options.en: The curator plans to replace the cupboard before examining any of its details.
options.zh: 策展人打算還未查看細節，就先換掉櫃子。

listening.explanationZh: 痕跡支持使用經歷，卻未提供修補者姓名；策展人計劃查問，不是未看細節就換櫃。

reply.promptZh: 策展人為甚麼暫時不寫修補者的人名？
reply.promptEn: Why is the curator not naming the repairers yet?

options.en: The repairs tell a story of use, but do not identify the people who made them.
options.zh: 修補呈現了使用經歷，但沒有指明由誰完成。

options.en: The visible traces establish maintenance, not which volunteer carried out each part.
options.zh: 可見痕跡顯示曾經維護，卻沒有說每個部分由哪位義工處理。

options.en: Former volunteers may know something that the worn handles alone cannot supply.
options.zh: 昔日義工可能知道磨損把手本身不能提供的資訊。

options.en: Naming a repairer requires more information than the marks currently provide.
options.zh: 要寫出維修者姓名，需要比現有痕跡更多的資料。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋了物件細節為甚麼尚不足以支持姓名，同時承認可見使用痕跡仍有價值。

scene.promptZh: 日記封面的污漬顯示曾受潮，但還沒讀過內容；同學卻說，作者一定在下雨當天因失戀哭泣。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: The marks may tell a story of the diary’s condition, but do not establish that personal event or motive.
options.zh: 痕跡可能呈現日記的保存經歷，但沒有證實那個私人事件或動機。

options.en: The stain identifies the writer’s exact reason for crying.
options.zh: 污漬指明了作者哭泣的確切原因。

options.en: There is no reason to examine the pages because a stained cover cannot provide the complete account.
options.zh: 封面污漬不能提供完整經歷，所以沒有理由再看內頁。

scene.explanationZh: 受潮痕跡與私人情感動機需要分清；有限資訊仍可以成為繼續查閱的起點。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能從物件 tell a story 的比喻本身推論出來？

options.en: Details can suggest past use or change.
options.zh: 細節可以暗示過去的使用或改變。

options.en: Every person’s motive and every event are already known.
options.zh: 每個人的動機及每件事情，都已經知道。

options.en: Other testimony may clarify the object’s history.
options.zh: 其他證言可能釐清物件的經歷。

contrast.explanationZh: 呈現部分經歷，不等於已完整知道所有事件及動機。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴問：「看到修補痕跡，就可以直接寫是林先生做的嗎？」還沒有人認出維修者。哪個回應最好？

options.en: The repairs tell a story, but not yet that particular name; let us ask the former volunteers first.
options.zh: 修補呈現了一段經歷，但尚未支持那個特定人名；先問昔日義工吧。

options.en: I would name him now because he volunteered there, even though nobody has linked him to the repairs.
options.zh: 我會現在寫他，因為他曾在那裏做義工，雖然沒有人把他與修補連起來。

options.en: We should remove all mention of repairs until we know the person’s name.
options.zh: 在知道姓名之前，應刪掉所有有關修補的描述。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可以保留已看見的修補，但不添加未證實的姓名；不必因一項未知，就抹去已見的細節。

speaking.en: These marks tell a story about past use, but I would look for more evidence before naming the people behind them.
speaking.zh: 這些痕跡呈現過去使用的經歷，但寫出背後人物的姓名前，我會再找證據。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明痕跡支持甚麼，以及仍有甚麼未知。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：人物整理自己童年的畫冊，看到同一隻貓畫了很多遍，旁邊有祖父寫的鼓勵。你想以第一人稱旁白呈現練習及被支持的成長，不把畫冊當成全家每人的完整人生。用一至兩句英文寫實際旁白。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以畫冊中的反覆練習及鼓勵，寫出可用的第一人稱旁白；保留自己的記憶及細節，不用局部物件取代全家的完整經歷。

examples.en: These pages tell a story about the child I was: I drew the same cat again and again, with my grandfather’s encouragement beside it. Turning the pages, I can see practice and kindness sharing the same small space.
examples.zh: 這些頁面呈現了童年的我：同一隻貓，我畫了一遍又一遍，旁邊有祖父的鼓勵。翻着頁，我看見練習與善意共在同一片小空間。

examples.en: The repeated cats and his careful notes tell a story of how I kept trying. I cannot find our whole family history here, but I can recognise the support that made these attempts possible.
examples.zh: 反覆畫出的貓，及他用心寫的字句，呈現了我怎樣不斷嘗試。這裏沒有全家的完整歷史，但我認得那些讓嘗試成為可能的支持。

glossary.en: the support that made these attempts possible
glossary.zh: 讓這些嘗試成為可能的支持

takeaways.en: The patched sleeves tell a story of long use, though the label does not say who sewed them.
takeaways.zh: 補過的衣袖呈現長期使用的經歷，但標籤沒有說由誰縫補。

takeaways.en: The notes in the margins told a story of changing plans as the writer reconsidered the ending.
takeaways.zh: 作者重新考慮結尾時，頁邊筆記呈現了計劃改變的經過。

titleEn: moved from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony
titleZh: 從日常核心退到禮儀邊緣

target.pattern: \bmov(?:e|es|ed|ing) from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony\b

brief.meaningEn: Change from a central daily practice into a more limited practice associated with special ceremonies.
brief.meaningZh: 從日常生活中核心的做法，轉為範圍較小、主要與特別禮儀相關的做法。
brief.grammar: a practice has moved from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony. Centre and edges describe social role and frequency, not a literal move across a room.
brief.register: Extended creative spatial comparison from the guide, rather than a fixed dictionary idiom. It describes reduced everyday centrality; remaining ceremonial use can still matter deeply.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是完全消失或必定失去價值，也不指真的搬移位置；需要同時交代日常用途減退，以及禮儀用途仍然保留。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把禮儀中仍使用，當成每天仍使用；也不把較少使用當作所有人都不再珍惜。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體的前後用途解釋地位轉變，保留仍然存在的重要性。

listening.en: In the imagined town, shared bread has moved from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony: it is no longer part of ordinary meals, but families still prepare it to welcome a new household.
listening.zh: 在這個虛構小鎮，分享麵包的做法已從日常核心退到禮儀邊緣：它不再是普通用餐的一部分，但家人仍會準備麵包，歡迎一個新家庭。
listening.promptZh: 用途怎樣改變？哪些做法仍保留下來？

options.en: Ordinary meals no longer include it, while a household welcome still does.
options.zh: 普通用餐不再包括它，但歡迎新家庭時仍會準備。

options.en: The bread is still prepared for every ordinary meal and no ceremony.
options.zh: 每頓普通餐仍會準備這麵包，禮儀中卻不用。

options.en: Families have stopped preparing it even for the household welcome.
options.zh: 即使歡迎新家庭，家人也不再準備這麵包。

options.en: The account concerns moving the bread from one side of the kitchen to the other.
options.zh: 敘述是把麵包從廚房一邊搬到另一邊。

listening.explanationZh: 意象關乎日常地位及用途的改變，歡迎禮儀仍然保留；不是每日照舊、完全消失，或只是搬位置。

reply.promptZh: 作者為甚麼說分享麵包的地位改變了？
reply.promptEn: Why does the writer describe a change in the bread’s role?

options.en: It has moved from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony: ordinary meals omit it, but the welcome still includes it.
options.zh: 它已從日常核心退到禮儀邊緣：普通用餐不再有，歡迎場合卻仍包括它。

options.en: It is now prepared for a particular welcome rather than as part of the daily meal.
options.zh: 現在為特定的歡迎場合準備，而不再是每天用餐的一部分。

options.en: Its remaining use is ceremonial, while its ordinary place at the table has ended.
options.zh: 餘下用途屬於禮儀，它原有的日常餐桌地位已結束。

options.en: The account contrasts an everyday practice that has stopped with a special practice that continues.
options.zh: 敘述對比了已停止的日常做法，以及仍繼續的特別做法。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都用用途及頻率的對比解釋，不把範圍縮小當作完全消失。

scene.promptZh: 另一個虛構社群每天仍用一套敬語，典禮時也用；只知道這兩項用途，不能說它已退到禮儀邊緣。哪句最好？

options.en: It has not moved from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony in the stated sense, because daily use continues.
options.zh: 按這裏所指的意思，它未從日常核心退到禮儀邊緣，因為每日使用仍然繼續。

options.en: Its use at ceremonies shows that it has ceased to be used in daily conversation.
options.zh: 典禮中的使用，顯示它已不再用於日常談話。

options.en: Because daily use continues, its ceremonial use must have stopped.
options.zh: 因為日常使用仍在，所以禮儀用途必定已停止。

scene.explanationZh: 日常與典禮用途可以並存；這個意象需要日常核心地位減退，不能用其中一項用途抹去另一項。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能從「日常核心到禮儀邊緣」這個意象推論出來？

options.en: Everyday centrality has diminished.
options.zh: 日常生活中的核心地位已減退。

options.en: Nobody values the remaining ceremonial practice.
options.zh: 沒有人珍惜仍然保留的禮儀做法。

options.en: A special occasion can preserve a practice no longer used daily.
options.zh: 特別場合可以保留一種已不再每天使用的做法。

contrast.explanationZh: 使用範圍縮小不等於價值消失，也不能代表全體的感情。

dialogue.promptZh: 訪客問：「不再每天做，是否表示這麵包已完全消失？」歡迎新家庭時仍然會做。哪個回應最好？

options.en: It has moved from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony, but families still prepare it for that welcome.
options.zh: 它已從日常核心退到禮儀邊緣，但家人仍為那個歡迎場合準備麵包。

options.en: Yes, I would describe it as gone, even though the welcome still uses it.
options.zh: 是的，即使歡迎時仍使用，我也會把它描述成已經消失。

options.en: No change has occurred, since one special occasion is enough to count as daily use.
options.zh: 沒有任何改變，因為一個特別場合已足以算作每日使用。

dialogue.explanationZh: 直接保留日常用途減退，以及禮儀用途仍在的兩面，不改寫成已消失或每日照舊。

speaking.en: The practice has moved from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony, but its place in that welcome still matters to the family.
speaking.zh: 這做法已從日常核心退到禮儀邊緣，但在那個歡迎場合中的地位，仍然對家人重要。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再交代用途縮小，而不是價值完全消失。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：小說中的家庭只在一位成員正式離家時唱一首舊歌，祖母記得以前做家務時也常唱。孫女想在這次告別前問祖母，哪句歌詞最想保留，而不假裝它現在仍每天唱。用一至兩句英文寫孫女實際說的話。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出向祖母提問的實際對話，誠實保留用途改變，再邀請她選珍惜的歌詞；不擅自說全家感受相同，也不宣告日常用途已恢復。

examples.en: The song has moved from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony, but I want this farewell to carry something you remember. Which line would you most like us to keep when we sing it together?
examples.zh: 這歌已從日常核心退到禮儀邊緣，但我想讓這次告別帶着你記得的事情。一起唱時，你最想我們保留哪句歌詞？

examples.en: I know the song has moved from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony, rather than staying part of our chores. Before we sing goodbye, will you tell me which words matter most to you?
examples.zh: 我知道這歌已從日常核心退到禮儀邊緣，而不再是做家務的一部分。唱歌告別之前，你可否告訴我，哪些字句對你最重要？

glossary.en: which words matter most to you

takeaways.en: In the fictional village, the greeting moved from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony, surviving mainly at naming celebrations.
takeaways.zh: 在虛構村落，這種問候從日常核心退到禮儀邊緣，主要在命名慶典中保留下來。

takeaways.en: Their song moved from the centre of everyday life to the edges of ceremony, yet the grandmother still chose its final verse for the farewell.
takeaways.zh: 他們的歌從日常核心退到禮儀邊緣，但祖母仍選擇最後一節，用於這次告別。

brief.meaningEn: Gradually become weaker or less noticeable and eventually disappear.
brief.meaningZh: 逐漸變弱或較不明顯，最終消失。
brief.grammar: excitement/noise fades away; faded away; has not faded away. Notice negation and gradual change: not faded away means it has not disappeared, not that every feature is unchanged.
brief.register: Common phrasal verb for sounds, feelings and continuing practices. Specify the evidence and timescale; a pause or quieter expression need not establish disappearance.
brief.boundaryZh: 這包含逐漸減弱的過程，不是突然不見；尚未消失，也不保證一直同樣強烈或完全沒有改變。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能只因一次安靜就判定興趣消失，也不把仍有保留當作所有日常做法都沒有改變。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以不同時間的具體變化說明消退，辨認否定形式及仍持續的證據。

listening.en: The initial excitement faded away as the group’s messages became less frequent over several weeks, but one member still wanted to try again; she asked what had made joining difficult rather than assume nobody cared.
listening.zh: 幾周之間，群組訊息變得愈來愈少，最初的興奮逐漸消退；但一位成員仍想再試，她問大家參與有甚麼難處，而不假定沒有人在乎。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼在逐漸改變？哪些意願仍然存在？

options.en: The early enthusiasm weakened over weeks, while one member still expressed interest in trying again.
options.zh: 最初熱情在幾周內減弱，但仍有一位成員表示想再試。

options.en: All members suddenly stopped caring at exactly the same moment.
options.zh: 所有成員在完全同一刻，突然不再關心。

options.en: The messages grew more frequent, showing steadily rising enthusiasm.
options.zh: 訊息變得愈來愈頻密，顯示熱情持續上升。

options.en: A new session had already solved the participation difficulties before she asked about them.
options.zh: 她查問之前，新一節活動已解決所有參與困難。

listening.explanationZh: 幾周內訊息漸少是消退的線索，但仍有人想試；原因及下次活動的成效還未確定。

reply.promptZh: 說話者為甚麼認為最初的熱情逐漸減弱？
reply.promptEn: Why did the speaker describe the early enthusiasm as gradually weakening?

options.en: It faded away as the group’s messages became less frequent over several weeks.
options.zh: 群組訊息在幾周內愈來愈少，熱情也逐漸消退。

options.en: The regular signs of enthusiasm diminished over time rather than growing stronger.
options.zh: 原本經常出現的熱情跡象，隨時間減少，而不是變強。

options.en: The change involved a falling level of activity across weeks, not one quiet minute.
options.zh: 變化是幾周內的活動逐步減少，不是安靜了一分鐘。

options.en: Comparing the weeks showed less frequent engagement than at the beginning.
options.zh: 比較不同星期的情況，顯示參與不如最初那麼頻密。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以不同時間的減弱作解釋，不把一人仍有興趣說成全體熱情不變，或完全沒有關心。

scene.promptZh: 一首舊歌不再每天唱，但家人每年聚會仍唱，年輕成員也學會了；你可以說它沒有消失，卻不能說用途完全不變。哪句準確？

options.en: The song has not faded away, although its everyday role has changed.
options.zh: 歌並沒有消失，但它在日常生活中的地位已改變。

options.en: The annual singing establishes that every family still sings it daily.
options.zh: 每年唱一次，就確立每戶人家仍每天唱。

options.en: The account describes the song being forgotten completely, with no remaining performance.
options.zh: 敘述說，歌已完全被遺忘，沒有保留任何演唱。

scene.explanationZh: 否定消失，保留了仍在唱的證據；不表示每日照舊，也不能抹去年輕人已學會的事。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 fade away 的逐漸意思？

options.en: A sound can become quieter over time.
options.zh: 聲音可以隨時間變得較輕。

options.en: It must disappear suddenly without any weakening process.
options.zh: 它必須不經任何減弱過程，就突然消失。

options.en: Interest can lose intensity even if some concern remains.
options.zh: 即使仍有部分關心，興趣的強度也可以降低。

contrast.explanationZh: 逐漸減弱不是必定瞬間消失；要看實際過程，以及還剩下甚麼。

dialogue.promptZh: 成員問：「訊息少了，是否大家都不在乎？要不要直接關群？」仍有一人想再試。哪個回答最好？

options.en: The early excitement has faded away, but we should ask about the difficulties before deciding what the group wants next.
options.zh: 最初的興奮已消退，但決定小組下一步之前，應先問大家遇到甚麼難處。

options.en: Yes, fewer messages mean nobody has any interest, so there is nothing left to ask.
options.zh: 是的，訊息少就表示沒有人有興趣，所以沒有甚麼可再問。

options.en: We should announce that enthusiasm is unchanged because one person still wants to try.
options.zh: 因為一個人仍想試，我們應宣布大家的熱情完全沒有改變。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認整體漸弱，也保留個別仍想參與的情況；先問原因，不替全體斷定不在乎或完全沒變。

speaking.en: The excitement may fade away, but I want to ask what people need before assuming that a quieter response means nobody cares.
speaking.zh: 興奮可能會消退，但我想先問人們需要甚麼，而不是假定較安靜的回應就表示沒有人關心。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再保留逐漸變化及個別感受的差異。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫小說的最後一段。主角送朋友上船後留在碼頭，先聽見告別聲，之後只剩腳下水聲；你想用聲音漸退收尾，讓友情仍有延續感，不直接說朋友已不重要。用一至兩句英文寫實際旁白。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出有先後的聲音漸退及一個具體動作，讓告別聲減弱與關係仍可延續並存；不把聲音消失當作友情消失。

examples.en: Her friend’s calls faded away beyond the harbour wall until only the water beneath the pier remained. She folded the letter into her pocket, keeping their next meeting close even as the boat passed out of sight.
examples.zh: 朋友的呼喊越過港口圍牆逐漸遠去，最後只剩碼頭下的水聲。她把信摺進口袋；即使船已離開視線，仍把下次相見放在心上。

examples.en: The last goodbye began to fade away, leaving the soft water sounds around her feet. She touched the letter and turned towards home, carrying a promise the distance had not erased.
examples.zh: 最後的告別聲開始漸退，腳邊留下輕柔的水聲。她摸了摸信，轉身往家走，帶着一個距離未能抹去的承諾。

glossary.en: folded the letter into her pocket

takeaways.en: The laughter faded away down the corridor, while she stayed behind to finish the note.
takeaways.zh: 笑聲沿走廊逐漸遠去，她則留在後面寫完短箋。

takeaways.en: His early excitement began to fade away after several cancelled meetings, so he asked whether the group wanted to change its plans.
takeaways.zh: 幾次聚會取消後，他最初的興奮開始消退，於是問小組是否想改變計劃。

brief.meaningEn: The initial impression made on someone can influence their early judgement or response.
brief.meaningZh: 初次接觸留下的印象，可以影響別人起初的判斷或反應。
brief.grammar: first impressions count; first impressions count when someone arrives. Count means matter here, not add up numbers. First impressions can later be revised.
brief.register: Conventional saying about initial contact. Explain the features affecting the first response without treating appearance as a reliable complete assessment of character or quality.
brief.boundaryZh: 有影響不等於永遠正確、不能改變或唯一重要；印象可來自招呼、說明及求助是否方便，不只外觀。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要用第一眼取代最終能力評估，也不因日後可能改觀，就忽略初來者的需要。
brief.outcomeZh: 能解釋初次接觸的具體作用，同時保留後續體驗及修正判斷的空間。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: First impressions count when customers enter a hotel.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 52, table 2, row 2; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: First impressions count at our new reading group: a clear welcome and a named contact helped two newcomers ask questions, but we still needed to learn from their later visits rather than judge the whole group from one evening.
listening.zh: 在我們的新讀書會，第一印象有影響：清楚的歡迎及一位已清楚介紹姓名的聯絡人，幫兩位新來者提出問題；但我們仍需要了解他們後續到訪的經驗，而不只用一晚評價整個小組。
listening.promptZh: 初次歡迎安排有何作用？之後還需了解甚麼？

options.en: The welcome supported early questions, while later experience still mattered for judging the group.
options.zh: 歡迎安排幫助最初提問，但後續經驗仍會影響對小組的評價。

options.en: One good evening established that every future meeting would meet every need.
options.zh: 一晚順利，就確立日後每次聚會都會符合所有需要。

options.en: Only the colour of the room affected whether newcomers could ask questions.
options.zh: 只有房間顏色，影響新來者能否提出問題。

options.en: The named contact was introduced mainly to record attendance, rather than to help newcomers ask questions.
options.zh: 介紹聯絡人主要是為了記錄出席，而不是幫新來者提問。

listening.explanationZh: 具體幫助是讓新來者知道怎樣提問；首晚不保證長期體驗，也不是只看裝飾或只為記錄出席。

reply.promptZh: 小組為甚麼清楚介紹聯絡人？
reply.promptEn: Why did the group clearly introduce a contact person?

options.en: First impressions count, and knowing whom to ask helped newcomers take part from the start.
options.zh: 第一印象有影響；知道可以問誰，幫新來者從開始就參與。

options.en: A named contact made it easier to raise early questions.
options.zh: 知道聯絡人的姓名，令最初的問題較容易提出。

options.en: Newcomers could see a route to getting help instead of guessing whom to approach.
options.zh: 新來者可以看見求助渠道，不必猜應找誰。

options.en: The welcome reduced uncertainty about how to begin participating.
options.zh: 歡迎安排減少了如何開始參與的不確定。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以初到時的求助及參與作解釋，不是說所有未來體驗都已獲保證。

scene.promptZh: 訪客起初覺得一間簡單工作室太安靜，參與活動後，卻欣賞大家細心聆聽；你想同時承認初印象及後來修正。哪句最好？

options.en: First impressions count, but this visitor revised the initial judgement after taking part.
options.zh: 第一印象有影響，但這位訪客在參與後修正了初步判斷。

options.en: Her first concern about the quietness should outweigh what she later learned from participating.
options.zh: 她最初對安靜的顧慮，應比後來參與所得的體會更重要。

options.en: The later appreciation means there was never any early uncertainty about the quiet room.
options.zh: 後來的欣賞，表示她起初從未對安靜房間感到疑慮。

scene.explanationZh: 第一印象有影響，也可以被新經驗修正；不讓舊顧慮壓過實際體驗，也不抹去最初曾有疑問的階段。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能從 first impressions count 推論出來？

options.en: Initial contact can influence a response.
options.zh: 初次接觸可以影響反應。

options.en: An early judgement can never be changed by later experience.
options.zh: 初步判斷永遠不能被後續經驗改變。

options.en: A clear welcome can matter alongside the activity itself.
options.zh: 清楚的歡迎，跟活動本身一樣可能有影響。

contrast.explanationZh: 有影響不等於不能修正，也不表示只有第一印象重要。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「首晚反應好，就不用再問新來者下次覺得怎樣吧？」目前沒有後續回饋。哪個回應最好？

options.en: First impressions count, but let us still ask about their later visits before claiming the arrangement works throughout.
options.zh: 第一印象有影響，但在稱安排一直有效前，仍要了解他們後續到訪的經驗。

options.en: Yes, a positive welcome is enough to assess all their future experiences.
options.zh: 是的，正面的首次歡迎，已足以評估他們日後所有體驗。

options.en: We should ignore the welcome entirely, since people might change their views later.
options.zh: 既然人們日後可能改變看法，我們就應完全忽略歡迎安排。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認首次安排的作用，也保留後續回饋的必要；不以一次保證全部，也不完全抹去第一印象。

speaking.en: First impressions count, but I want our welcome to be followed by the same clear help during later visits.
speaking.zh: 第一印象有影響，但我希望首次歡迎之後，後續到訪也有同樣清楚的幫助。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把初次接觸與持續體驗連起來。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你第一次跟新伙伴合作時打斷了她，她現在較少發言。你想承認最初印象有影響，為打斷道歉，並在下次討論先聽她完整說完，不要求她立即改變看法。用一至兩句英文寫真實道歉。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出承認自己行為的道歉，以及可以觀察的下一步；不要求對方立即原諒或改觀，也不只談裝飾或外貌。

examples.en: First impressions count, and I am sorry I interrupted you in our first discussion. Next time I will let you finish before responding, without expecting you to change your view of me immediately.
examples.zh: 第一印象有影響，對不起，我在第一次討論時打斷了你。下次我會等你說完再回應，不期望你立即改變對我的看法。

examples.en: I know first impressions count, so I should acknowledge how my interruptions affected our start. I would like to listen to your full idea at the next meeting and earn your trust through how I respond.
examples.zh: 我知道第一印象有影響，所以應承認我的打斷怎樣影響了我們的開始。下次聚會，我想聽你完整的想法，再以自己的回應逐漸取得信任。

glossary.en: change your view of me immediately

takeaways.en: First impressions count, so she greeted the new volunteers clearly and showed them whom to ask for help.
takeaways.zh: 第一印象有影響，所以她清楚歡迎新義工，並告訴他們可以向誰求助。

takeaways.en: He knew first impressions count, but he listened again before letting one awkward introduction define his new colleague.
takeaways.zh: 他知道第一印象有影響，但仍再次聆聽，不讓一次尷尬介紹就定義了新同事。
